chapters.title: Chapter 601: Poison Revenge (2) [Bonus]
paragraphs: Chaos erupted everywhere when the war alarms sounded in Vale. They were already running before the alarms went off.
However, hearing them now, they knew the situation had turned dire, so they started running frantically.
Some tried to use the teleportation gate in Vale City, but when they got there, they found out they were not working.

Strangely, the teleportation gates were not working. That was the most chilling thing they all encountered. The rain was falling, the poisonous acid was melting people, and the screams filled the air, yet the teleportation gates were not working.
However, as the seconds passed, people started to notice something.
"Why am I not dead when the poison rain definitely fell on me?" one of them asked.
"Me too... I am alive."
"I am the same. What does this mean?"

Those who started to notice they were still alive despite the poison falling on them began to wonder. A few clever ones started examining the bodies of their friends who had died, and within a minute, the answer became clear.

"These are all people from the Vale and Wilson noble families," one of them said, causing the others to look even deeper. When they did, they all came to the same conclusion: The people dying were all from the Vale and Wilson noble families.
"But why would the Poison Wicked Witch attack them? Aren’t they on good terms or something?" Many became puzzled, so instead of finding ways to run, they now wanted to get to the bottom of things.
It’s human nature to be curious. Despite the danger surrounding them, they first wanted to understand what was happening and, if possible, uncover the root of things.
Humans are just creatures that can’t be understood, regardless of gender.
Soon, the sky cleared, and the Poison Witch, who had now taken her true form as the once princess of the Deckling noble family, the royals of the Kyrrith kingdom 200 years ago, showed herself.
When the onlookers saw her, they became even more puzzled.

"Who is she? I thought this was a battle between the kingdom and the Poison Wicked Witch... who is this lady?" they wondered, but their answer soon came when thousands of soldiers clad in metallic armor, wielding powerful weapons, started surrounding her.

Some held spears that could easily pierce heaven-grade armor and swords that could cut through the most formidable defenses. The archers were even equipped with better arrows that could deal a deadly blow.
"Aim!" One of the generals leading the Archer unit shouted. Everyone was in the air, facing off against Princess Lovina.
There wasn’t even a warning from the generals, who had managed to send the king away before coming after Princess Lovina.
They had been preparing for this day for a very long time, so once they ensured their king was out of harm’s way, they came to finish the job.
They were confident, despite their opponent being someone on the same level as a kingdom protector. They had prepared well, so they were not afraid of her.
However, when the archers aimed and were about to fire, Princess Lovina waved her staff and muttered two words:
"Poison Explosion."

The arrowheads exploded, sending thousands of archers hurtling down. The moment they landed hard on the ground, their bodies turned black, showing they had died from poison, and it had corroded their flesh.
"Throw your weapon—" The general who shouted the command wasn’t even done when more explosions erupted, sending more soldiers flying down. The swordsmen and spearmen all went down.
Even those wielding staffs weren’t any better. They all died from the single explosion of their weapons, shocking anyone watching the battle from outside or inside the city.
Unlike the start of the battle, when only a select few died, everyone wielding weapons died this time. It wasn’t just those who had the blood of the Vale and Wilson noble families.
The explosion was a decisive move, planned and executed to perfection. Princess Lovina had been planning her vengeance for a very long time.
She knew she was outnumbered, so she made sure to gain the upper hand one way or another.
Thankfully, her reputation as a Pill Saint and the wicked Poison Witch made her someone the Kyrrith kingdom relied on.
Because they needed her poisonous services so much, she ensured they listened to her suggestions, which is how they ended up in this mess.
She made sure their weapons were loaded and coated in her poison, which in fact was a skill that today allowed her to explode said laced weapons with a swing of her staff.
King Vale, who was watching from a distance, immediately ordered the men manning the other weapons to throw them away.
However, Princess Lovina had long made her move, killing over fifty thousand soldiers within a few seconds.
It was safe to say they trusted the wrong person, which cost them greatly.
The only ones left were the seven generals.
Now, the only thing they could do was face her themselves, using none of her weapons. However, they were afraid. The seven generals were so scared.
"What are you idiots waiting for? Attack her! Reinforcements will be here soon," King Vale said, causing his seven generals to charge.
Naturally, they had good reason to worry, considering what they had just witnessed.
So the fear in their hearts made them hesitate, and that hesitation was enough for Princess Lovina to gain the upper hand.
She unleashed a powerful spell that conjured five poison snakes and attacked the generals.
Unfortunately, they couldn’t defend against it because of their fear, so they succumbed to the attack. But the other two attackers pressed from both her left and right, pushing her back.

They continued to push her back, doing their best to stay alive until reinforcements arrived. But that didn’t last long, because before they could approach her after their tenth attack, a poison mist enveloped them, and like ants eating sugar, they were consumed by the fog.
However, Princess Lovina’s face paled slightly, showing she had used more than she could for that last attack. So she moved in, wanting to kill the main person she came for—King Vale.
He was the one who led the massacre on her family 200 years ago... so she wanted him dead. Even if she only manages to kill him and not the others, she will consider it a success...
However, just as she was closing the distance, a figure appeared and stopped her. This figure was at the fourth level of the Core Formation stage.
She stopped in her tracks, knowing the variables she calculated had arrived. She looked up at the figure, and as she expected, it was someone she knew would come.

"Kingdom Protector Nathan, I would like you to know you swore to protect my family hundreds of years ago, but you never showed when it came to it. So stay out of my way and let me get my revenge," Princess Lovina said, her eyes cold.

chapters.title: Chapter 602: Poison Revenge (3) [Bonus]
paragraphs: "I am afraid I can’t do that." Kingdom Protector Nathan said, taking out his sword. Behind him, hundreds of Peak Sovereigns and a few Core formation experts appeared.
There were even three peak core formation experts in the fold. This was a clear sign that the four kingdom protectors weren’t the strongest.
There are hidden gems, and it seems they are all in this together.
"So you all are in this together...even you, Grandpa," Princess Lovina said, looking toward a bald man who seemed to be in his late 60s. He is one of the three Peak Core formation experts.

"Sorry, little girl. If your father had listened to reason and handed over the Dream crystal, none of this would have happened. Thankfully, you are here now, so why don’t you hand over that necklace around your neck?" the old man said with a smile.
Princess Lovina turned and looked at the necklace around her neck, focusing on the crystal inside a small golden circle. It looked almost like a diamond, and the shine coming from it looked dreamy.

"So because of this, you killed every last person of the Deckling family." Princess Lovine bit her lips, her blood boiling as she looked past Kingdom Protector Nathan, locking gaze with her grandpa, who once carried her on his neck and played with her.
Just remembering those fond memories seems to make her blood boil even more.
"Yes. Your father and mother wouldn’t hand that thing over, and since it can’t be forcefully taken, I will advise you to hand it over, girl.

The path of cultivation is a torturous one. If they had listened and handed over the crystal, everything would have ended well for them. Perhaps they would be alive today. So don’t make the same mistake your parent made."
The Dream Crystal was something that was discovered in the ancient battlefield of Parting. It was said to hold the dream of an immortal who once lived in this world.
Inside the dream is the location of his hidden treasures, which he left behind before he ascended.
Princess Lovina’s father found it on one of his explorations in the ancient battlefield of parting, but his cultivation base wasn’t high enough to view the dream of an immortal, so he held on to it.

However, the evil men always want what doesn’t belong to them, so they came after it. When he refused to hand it over, they started to use force. Perhaps they thought killing a few would compel him to hand it over.

But he didn’t, and since they can’t be forcefully taken unless Lovina’s father hands it over, they killed everyone, even killing him in the hope that after he died, the Dream Crystal would pick someone else.

However, when the massacre ended and they checked, the Dream crystal was long gone, making their massacre a pointless one. But now, what they spent hundreds of years looking for was now right in front of them.

Princess Lovina’s eyes filled with tears, knowing she had lost everything because of a trinket. Then, she grabbed the dream crystal, and before anyone could move, she crashed it, causing everyone to turn pale.
"What did you do?" Princess Lovina’s grandpa shouted.
"I got my revnge, you old bastard. No wonder mom always called you an ugly, useless, good-for-nothing, lazy, wasteful person who doesn’t have his priorities straight.
You are a disgrace to all grandpas. Why am I even calling you that...you don’t deserve such a title, you ugly thing calling himself a human"
"Kill her." The old man’s blood was boiling so much that blood started seeping from the core of his eyes.
Protector Nathan stabbed his sword forward, aiming to end Princess Lovina’s life. Of course, she made no attempts to dodge. The revenge she wanted went better than she had hoped.
The hopes of everyone who was after the Dream Crystal were crushed in her palm, which felt good. So she was ready to die. Not that she could survive the force she was up against.

Protector Nathan’s sword, coated in sword qi, was stabbed toward her. However, just when the sword could touch her, a kick came out of nowhere and landed on Protector Nathan’s face, sending him flying.
"Why don’t you pick someone your own size?" Vari said, appearing in front of Princess Lovina. The next second, a chilling laughter entered everyone’s ears.
The suddenly, Lani appeared behind, Princess Lovina’s grand father laughing like a maniac as she slit his throat. She vanished and appeared beside Vari, who smirked,
"Show off," She said
"Only if the showing off is dope as fuck." They are not wearing masks, so everyone who knows them immediately recognises them despite their appearance being enhanced after the True Name awakening.
"That is the Auction Master, Lady Lani...what is she doing here?" One of the onlookers asked.

"Why did you ask that when you saw and heard what happened. The Joker has finally made her identity known." Even before her true name awakening, she was known as the Joker, but nobody aside from her master knew her true identity.
Now, everyone knows, and the shock it brought them was just too much.
"AAAARRHHHGG"

Ten people suddenly dropped from the air, screaming, clinging to their heads as they rolled on the floor. Suddenly, thorns burst from their stomachs, and red flowers grew on them, turning their bodies into fertilizer.
Elaine appeared calmly in the air, petals falling from her. Her aura was manifesting as red petals, which made the sudden death of ten Sovereigns both beautiful and chilling.
But while the three ladies made a rather good entrance, Val appeared, and the scene changed.
The moon appeared in the sky, and when she appeared, she immediately swung her sword, sending a wide, half-moon-shaped arc at the reinforcement.
In an instant, hundreds of them were bathed in the moon’s radiance, incinerating their bodies.
"Val, we all agreed to kill not less than 20, why go all out from the start?" Vari glared at the silver-haired beauty who appeared in the air.
"Sorry, I didn’t expect them to be this weak," Val responded nonchalantly.
Her sisters just chucked, but the next second, the void cracked and hundreds of spears rained from it. Yet again, hundreds of soldiers lost their lives as Ingrid appeared smiling.
Vari and her sister just shrugged. By the time the last of them appeared, only two of the remaining Peak Core formation experts, Protector Nathan and King Vale, remained.

chapters.title: Chapter 603: Poison Revenge (4)
paragraphs: Nobody knows where they came from, but like grim reapers, they appear, killing left, right, and center, disregarding their realms and levels. They don’t even bother to make it seem obvious; they just come and start killing.

Ingrid came with the void, raining down spears on them like the tide. Then Lilian arrived, raining down fire. She didn’t take her ice form simply because she had become very powerful in her fire form.

This was due to the Starfire Herb that Vexthra got for her. In addition to the other herbs she added, her flame element had already reached the Super level, just a step away from reaching the Perfect stage.
She was terrifying and powerful with fire. Her flame element consumed everyone when she came, killing hundreds, just like Val did.
When all fifteen of them arrived, the onlookers were left with their jaws hanging. It was the most bizarre thing they had ever seen.
The most shocking part was that when the onlookers recognised some of the Kent’s women, they became puzzled. The ladies are now beautiful beyond measure.
Aside from their beauty, they were also very powerful—monstrous, even. Their abnormality made the onlookers start to question just what the hell was going on.
"I don’t even seem to recognize Senior Sister Val anymore. She has changed," one of the onlookers, a lady, said, looking at Val with admiration.
She held a sword, and her uniform showed she was from the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect, the sect from which Val came.
Others also recognized some of the ladies, like Alina, whom many knew from the annual auction, and Selene, who they knew as one of the Sword Saintesses, not forgetting Neomi, the Spear Saintess.
However, when their eyes landed on Velyra, they started to wonder.
"I never knew humans could have red skin."
"Stupid head, humans don’t have red skin. She is clearly a demon..."
"Maybe she is a red dragon. I learned that the flame dragons—some are red."
"Maybe, but damn, is she beautiful. I never knew people with red skin could be this beautiful."
"...Suddenly, I feel like spraying my skin red."
"Me too."
"...Count me in."

But while the humans were drooling over Velyra’s beauty, Princess Lovina, who had been prepared to die, was now in shock, looking at the ladies who had, in a strange way, formed a circle around her, not even paying attention to the four left to kill.
They were not worried that they would escape. They couldn’t, because Alina made sure of that. She sealed the space so that no one could get away.
"Who are you, ladies?" Princess Lovina managed to ask. Perhaps in her shocked state, she didn’t recognize some familiar faces—not that she should be blamed for that.
The ladies standing around her and smiling are just too strange for her to recognise them easily in her current state.
So she asked the most obvious question. However, this question caused the ladies to wonder about many things.

The question sounded like they should tell her their code name, something like "The Dangerous Harem," "The Dangerous Vixens," "The Demolishers," or the like. But they didn’t have one, so they just smiled.
"Kent sent us to come get you," Vari answered, knowing that was the quickest way to make her trust them. After all, she was acquainted with Kent.
"Kent...?" Princess Lovina became puzzled.
"Yes. He said, and I quote, ’You can’t die until you are done serving him for the 100 years you promised.’" The ladies laughed.

They were planning the adventures they would go on after awakening their primordial spirits when Kent came to tell them he had a mission for them. This brought them so much joy that they started jumping around.
They were like children hearing Santa was coming to the mall. So getting to come out and fight was a dream come true for them.
"The agreement was ten years," Princess Lovina said, keeping a straight face despite her shocked state.
"Take the addition of ninety years as payment for us saving your life. And before you say you were prepared to die, know that death doesn’t want you... Isn’t that right, Elaine?"
"You’re on point, big sister; death doesn’t want her... If she doesn’t believe it, she can try dying now and see whether she will remain dead."
Princess Lovina looked at the ladies for a few seconds before a sigh escaped her lips. "Fine, but I won’t stay a day after the hundred years."
Kent’s women smiled upon hearing that.
"So, who is going to take care of them?" Lilian asked, looking at the four they were left to kill.
"Leave that bastard to me." Without even waiting to hear their protest, Princess Lovina lunged at King Vale and swung her staff at him.
The ladies sighed, then moved—well, only three of them moved.
Lani, Velyra, and Vari.
Lani took on one of the Peak Core Formation experts, and Velyra took the other. As for Vari, she went after Protector Nathan, who nearly killed her the last time they fought.

Though she managed to knock him unconscious, the bastard had hurt her badly, so this time, she wanted revenge. Since her hair had turned white, it was a purposeful vengeance. She wouldn’t stop until he was dead.
The rest of the ladies moved closer to Princess Lovina’s fighting area to ensure she didn’t miraculously die. Thankfully, after an hour, all the battles ended.
King Vale was impaled through the chest, killing him instantly. Of course, he had suffered from the poison so badly that when he died, it could be considered mercy.
As for Protector Nathan, Vari killed him using one of her bloodline abilities, [Death by a Thousand Cuts]. He suffered before dying.
Once everything was over, the ladies took Lovina away, leaving a dead silence in their wake. Vari even made sure to remind them that Kent sent his regards.
But that wasn’t the shocking part. After the battle ended and the dead were checked, it was found that not a single innocent person had died aside from the soldier..
This made many wonder just how much someone could hate an entire family to the point that they would create spells tailored solely to their bloodline.
It was a shocker, and when they learned the ladies were all wives of the most wanted fugitive in the four kingdoms, everyone wiped the idea of going after him for the reward money.
They valued their lives more than money. They asked themselves, "If the wives are this monstrous, what about their husbands?"
Nobody wants to look for that answer, so just like that, Kent changed from the most wanted fugitive to the most dangerous person in the four kingdoms — well, three and a half kingdoms now.

"I don’t even seem to recognize Senior Sister Val anymore.
She has changed," one of the onlookers, a lady, said, looking at Val with admiration.
She held a sword, and her uniform showed she was from the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect, the sect from which Val came.
Others also recognized some of the ladies, like Alina, whom many knew from the annual auction, and Selene, who they knew as one of the Sword Saintesses, not forgetting Neomi, the Spear Saintess.
However, when their eyes landed on Velyra, they started to wonder.
"I never knew humans could have red skin."
"Stupid head, humans don’t have red skin.
She is clearly a demon..."
"Maybe she is a red dragon.
I learned that the flame dragons—some are red."
"Maybe, but damn, is she beautiful.
I never knew people with red skin could be this beautiful."
"...Suddenly, I feel like spraying my skin red."
"Me too."
"...Count me in."

But while the humans were drooling over Velyra’s beauty, Princess Lovina, who had been prepared to die, was now in shock, looking at the ladies who had, in a strange way, formed a circle around her, not even paying attention to the four left to kill.
They were not worried that they would escape.
They couldn’t, because Alina made sure of that.
She sealed the space so that no one could get away.
"Who are you, ladies?" Princess Lovina managed to ask.
Perhaps in her shocked state, she didn’t recognize some familiar faces—not that she should be blamed for that.
The ladies standing around her and smiling are just too strange for her to recognise them easily in her current state.
So she asked the most obvious question.
However, this question caused the ladies to wonder about many things.
The question sounded like they should tell her their code name, something like "The Dangerous Harem," "The Dangerous Vixens," "The Demolishers," or the like.
But they didn’t have one, so they just smiled.
"Kent sent us to come get you," Vari answered, knowing that was the quickest way to make her trust them.
After all, she was acquainted with Kent.
"Kent...?" Princess Lovina became puzzled.
"Yes.
He said, and I quote, ’You can’t die until you are done serving him for the 100 years you promised.’" The ladies laughed.
They were planning the adventures they would go on after awakening their primordial spirits when Kent came to tell them he had a mission for them.
This brought them so much joy that they started jumping around.
They were like children hearing Santa was coming to the mall.
So getting to come out and fight was a dream come true for them.
"The agreement was ten years," Princess Lovina said, keeping a straight face despite her shocked state.
"Take the addition of ninety years as payment for us saving your life.
And before you say you were prepared to die, know that death doesn’t want you...
Isn’t that right, Elaine?"
"You’re on point, big sister; death doesn’t want her...
If she doesn’t believe it, she can try dying now and see whether she will remain dead."
Princess Lovina looked at the ladies for a few seconds before a sigh escaped her lips.
"Fine, but I won’t stay a day after the hundred years."
Kent’s women smiled upon hearing that.
"So, who is going to take care of them?" Lilian asked, looking at the four they were left to kill.
"Leave that bastard to me." Without even waiting to hear their protest, Princess Lovina lunged at King Vale and swung her staff at him.
The ladies sighed, then moved—well, only three of them moved.
Lani, Velyra, and Vari.
Lani took on one of the Peak Core Formation experts, and Velyra took the other.
As for Vari, she went after Protector Nathan, who nearly killed her the last time they fought.
Though she managed to knock him unconscious, the bastard had hurt her badly, so this time, she wanted revenge.
Since her hair had turned white, it was a purposeful vengeance.
She wouldn’t stop until he was dead.
The rest of the ladies moved closer to Princess Lovina’s fighting area to ensure she didn’t miraculously die.
Thankfully, after an hour, all the battles ended.
King Vale was impaled through the chest, killing him instantly.
Of course, he had suffered from the poison so badly that when he died, it could be considered mercy.
As for Protector Nathan, Vari killed him using one of her bloodline abilities, [Death by a Thousand Cuts].
He suffered before dying.
Once everything was over, the ladies took Lovina away, leaving a dead silence in their wake.
Vari even made sure to remind them that Kent sent his regards.
But that wasn’t the shocking part.
After the battle ended and the dead were checked, it was found that not a single innocent person had died aside from the soldier..
This made many wonder just how much someone could hate an entire family to the point that they would create spells tailored solely to their bloodline.
It was a shocker, and when they learned the ladies were all wives of the most wanted fugitive in the four kingdoms, everyone wiped the idea of going after him for the reward money.
They valued their lives more than money.
They asked themselves, "If the wives are this monstrous, what about their husbands?"
Nobody wants to look for that answer, so just like that, Kent changed from the most wanted fugitive to the most dangerous person in the four kingdoms — well, three and a half kingdoms now.

chapters.title: Chapter 604: Welcome to the Tower
paragraphs: While his wives were away fighting, Kent was in the mountain garden wrestling with Gaia, Dori, and Akira.

Gaia created a wrestling ring for them, so they truly indulged in the wrestling fantasy inside the mountain garden. No one could blame them. They were just spending time together, and since everyone was happy, the fun continued.
Kent was losing miserably.
⟪I can’t believe you are this weak, master... Makes me wonder where all your bragging was coming from,⟫
Gaia said, holding one of Kent’s legs up while her body leaned on him. She was clad in designer sportswear, showing professionalism.
Akira struck the ground three times, and since Kent couldn’t move, it signaled she was the winner.
"I am strong; it’s just that you three are monsters. That’s why I keep losing." Kent sighed, his expression defeated. This made the three lolis smile, showing satisfaction in defeating their master.
⟪Don’t cry, master. One of these days, you’ll rise to our level, and perhaps by then, you won’t look defeated after we beat you miserably.⟫ Dori and her sisters giggled.
Kent just sat down and smiled.
He could tell his three assistants were genuinely happy defeating him. It was weird because they were very happy, and he didn’t know if they truly were billions of years old.
Whenever they defeated him, the satisfaction, the smile, and the genuinely ecstatic expression said it all; they were thrilled, and that strangely made him very happy.
Though he was playing pretend, their happiness said everything he needed to know. Kent looked at the three sisters and smiled.
"Akira, you’re next," he called out, and Akira came running. She was throwing punches in the air and moving her legs like a professional wrestler.
Gaia came to officiate. Soon, the battle was underway. Akira grabbed Kent’s leg and pulled it forward. Of course, Kent had to fall, so he faked tripping and fell back.
However, before landing on the ground, Akira jumped up and slammed him to the ground using her elbow, which looked very funny given her body size.
Akira stood up and ran to the side of the ring, slamming her body against the spring ropes. The momentum gathered from the slam pushed her even faster to create more force.
Then, when she gathered enough momentum, she moved and slammed her body into Kent, making the shameless Chaos Dragon make hurtful sounds.
Akira smiled and dragged him to the center of the ring, laying him down. She then climbed to the third rope and jumped high into the air, and came down, slamming hard on Kent’s body.
Then she grabbed his leg and leaned on him.
Gaia moved, sliding across the surface of the rubber floor.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
She slammed her tiny palm on the floor three times. Kent didn’t even make a single move as Akira held him down throughout the three strikes.

When she let him go, Kent lazily threw his hand, striking the floor, and lay on his back, gazing at the blue sky with a defeated expression. Akira and her sisters were jumping up and down, celebrating yet another win.
A couple of meters away, Kent’s women were left gobsmacked as they stood frozen, looking at what could be said to be the most shocking thing they had ever seen in their entire lives.
However, while one would think they were shocked watching Kent get defeated, their focus wasn’t on that. Instead, they are fascinated by the game Kent and his three assistants were playing.
"What is this game?" Vari muttered in a dazed tone, looking at the wrestling ring.
⟪Big sister, do you want to play? Master is too weak for experts like us,⟫ Gaia said, looking at Kent’s women.
"What is this game?" she asked, sounding louder this time.
⟪It’s called wrestling. Do you want to try it? We promise we won’t disgrace you like we did with Master,⟫ Dori said, raising the scout’s honor symbol.
By then, Kent lifted himself and sat inside the ring, smiling at his wives.
"It’s a game from my world called wrestling. All you have to do is weaken your opponent and press their back to the ground. If, after three strikes, they can’t move, you win."
"Sounds fun," Unity jumped into the ring, ready to show her strength. However, the moment she landed inside, something happened.
"I can’t feel my cultivation base," Unity said.
"Yeah. The ring locks everything, turning you into a mortal."
Gaia made sure all grounds were covered when she made the ring. It takes one’s cultivation base away, leaving them with only their mortal strength...
[Unity, dear, make sure they win in the end.] Kent used the harem connection to talk to Unity, who smiled and understood the assignment.
Dori climbed into the ring, and just like with Kent, the battle started, causing the ladies who had never seen something like this to become ecstatic. They all wanted to try it.
After a few more minutes, Dori defeated Unity, doing a backflip to celebrate. Lilian jumped into the ring next, facing off against the feisty Gaia, who also defeated her opponent.

She gave Lilian the classic ’you can’t see me’ celebration, causing Kent to smile as he watched all this. Just like that, all his women joined the wrestling, bringing a warm atmosphere to the mountain garden.
This was all he wanted—an environment filled with love and happiness. He was getting some, and the feeling was just too much to describe.
Kent spent a few minutes making sure his ladies understood the back-and-forth before walking toward the shocked princess, who couldn’t decide where to focus her attention.
When she turned left, the city lay before her like a river.
The elegant city of humans featured many towering glassy buildings, futuristic designs, and calm sights that would never tire the eye.
Then, away from such a beautiful city, the red city loomed afar from where she stood, yet she could feel the elegance deep in her bones.
She did not seem to hate it one bit, and seeing the redskin beings moving about, playing with the humans and doing all kinds of things, many thoughts passed through her mind.
But if she looked away and focused on the wrestling match, that alone made her wonder just where in the cosmos she had found herself.
"So, this is the real you, huh... not bad for the Poison Wicked Witch." Kent approached her with a smile.
"By the way, welcome to the tower."

chapters.title: Chapter 605: Meeting Sword King Shawn [Bonus]
paragraphs: "What is this place?" Princess Lovina asked, looking puzzled.
"This is a secret world I own. You can think of it as a pocket world," Kent replied. The wrestling match between his three assistants and his women continued joyfully.
Meanwhile, he stood to the side, talking to Princess Lovina. Until a few hours ago, everybody knew her as the Wicked Poison Witch, one of the seven Pill Saints—until Kent killed a couple of them.

Not that they didn’t deserve it. However, the Wicked Poison Witch turns out to be more than just a wicked lady who doesn’t care who she poisons. She turns out to be more than a wicked witch, but a Princess, or was once a princess.
Princess Lovina stood there in a daze.
The discovery that she was in a new world outside Sonox, or perhaps hidden within Sonox—not that it was important, but the fact that she was in a new world—shocked her.

The display—from the human city named Gaiaville to the Blood City, which is inhabited by the Bloodvein tribe, and back to the wrestling ring—was just too much for her medieval cultivation world mindset to comprehend.
Looking at her stunned expression, Kent smiled.
"You will get used to it soon enough... In any case, the spiritual qi here is much denser and purer than the outside, so use it to solidify your cultivation base before your foundation is destroyed."
Princess Lovina nodded, hearing what Kent said.
She anticipated that today would be the end of her life, but it turned out her life was much harder, and this was thanks to Kent, who sent his women to intervene at the crucial moment.
Now, for Kent helping her cure the poison that had plagued her for hundreds of years, she promised to become his servant for ten years, but now she will serve him for 100 years.
"Thank you for saving my life... again," Princess Lovina said with a small smile.
The old, ragged woman known as the wicked Poison Witch was nowhere to be seen, and now news of her being the long-dead princess of Kyrrith had spread everywhere.
It caused a great deal of mayhem, considering many never expected her to have such a background. But in the end, they had to come to terms with it...
Kent smiled. "Don’t worry about it. I just did what I felt was right. But the fact that you thought only you could take down an entire kingdom is just too shocking... What were you thinking?
I know you spent years planning your revenge, but you had to have known that kingdoms aren’t as simple as they appear.
You had to have known you would fail in killing everyone... If that is the case, then perhaps you planned on dying alongside the ones you went to kill?
"I don’t know about you, but when it comes to revenge, I like to finish them off and go back to my bed and sleep, not dying in the end.
Using your life to get revenge is not revenge; it’s just plain stupidity."
Princess Lovina sighed.
In truth, she had known her plan wouldn’t succeed simply because she suspected the danger she was facing wasn’t something she could win. However, she also had other plans.
That last-minute attack that could have claimed her life was also her final move to kill everyone, including the Core Formation experts.
Her core was loaded with poison that she planned to detonate. Had she succeeded, she would have killed all of them, and Vale City would have become uninhabitable for hundreds of years.
So, in a twisted kind of way, she actually planned on dying to unleash her strongest move.
But now, hearing Kent’s words, she couldn’t help but wonder if she was just being stupid, putting her life on the line.
"Ah... don’t worry about it. You are safe now; that is the only important thing." Kent sighed and then called out to Dori.
"Get dressed, Dori, we are going somewhere." Dori nodded and blinked away. A few seconds later, she came back wearing all black.

"Dori, we are not going to a funeral at Coachella, so why are you dressed like an up-and-coming goth queen?" Dori was clad in black trousers, a hoodie, and even some stylish shoes, almost giving Yeezy a run for their money.
⟪We are going out, so I need to dress to impress,⟫ Dori smiled, saying that. Kent just smirked and waved at his women.
"I am going out. When done, show Princess Lovina here around." They waved back. Kent and Dori then vanished and appeared somewhere near Vastport City.
Kent retrieved a carriage, and they left Vastport City, heading toward Eldorath, in the northern part of the human continent.
⟪Where are we going, master?⟫ Dori asked.
"We are going to see a friend of mine. He needs my help, and I think you can help him get it," Kent responded.

After a while, they entered the borders of the Eldorath Kingdom. Just as the Athea Kingdom is known for commerce, buying, and selling, the Eldorath Kingdom is known for producing food, minerals, and clothing.

They are the fashion kingdom and a rather nice place to be if you are fond of fashion. Basically, everyone there is either a fashion icon or a fashion designer. They make the best clothes, down to the finest armor.
However, Kent and Dori weren’t going there for the fashion. He was going to meet with Sword King Shawn, whom he had promised to meet a month ago.
They didn’t enter Eldor City. Instead, they moved higher into the mountains until they came to a stop at a stone platform featuring a large statue of a man holding a sword.
A few minutes after they arrived, Sword King Shawn also appeared.
"Good to see you again, Kent," Sword King Shawn said with a polite smile, shaking Kent’s hand.
"Good to see you too, Sword King Shawn... This is my assistant, Dori," Kent responded, introducing her.
"Oh, congratulations on your breakthrough. It looks like you moved to the third level of the Core Formation stage within a month."
Sword King Shawn nodded. "Thanks for helping me upgrade my spirit root to the immortal grade. It even helped my soul reach the Tier 11 stage."
Kent smiled. "In that case, why don’t we get going?" Kent retrieved the world teleporter and placed his hand on Sword King Shawn’s shoulder.
The next second, they vanished...

chapters.title: Chapter 606: Back To Fedora [Bonus]
paragraphs: The last time Kent came to Fedora was when he came to rescue Dori from the Crimson Vipers, an elite bandit group that worked for the Tyrant Orc King, Balma.
Fedora is a ’High World’ ruled by the Beastkins. There are eight Beast races, to be precise: the Tigerkin, Foxkin, Catkin, Rabbitkin, Lionkin, Batkin, Hellhounds, and the Orcs.
The Orc King Balma is the strongest in the land, and long before Dori arrived, his rule was supreme.
However, thanks to Dori’s schemes and planning, the Foxkin managed to break free from his rule when their leader, Hkum, became a Spirit Lord.
With her superior knowledge, she was able to attract the Tigerkin and perhaps the Catkin to their side, strengthening the rebel alliance.
Although the leaders of the Tigerkin and Catkin are not yet at the Spirit Lord stage, they are strong enough to fight one. So the Rebel Alliance was rising steadily.
However, things became dull after Dori and her two friends, one of whom was the Foxkin’s youngest princess, were captured.
Thankfully, Kent, his undead, and Veydris managed to poison Orc King Balma, rendering him incapable of fighting for the next few years.

Kent didn’t know what had happened since then; however, when Sword King Shawn asked him for help expanding and strengthening his sword realm, Kent knew adding him to the rebel alliance was the right move.

He had no problem bringing his undead to this world, but Kent didn’t want to do it simply because doing so would escalate the timeline that Dori had set. This was the main reason he didn’t want to send them there.
Per Dori’s calculation, a great war will happen within the next 15 years. However, Kent happened, and that timeline is now shaky.
The battle will start when the Orc King manages to force the poison out of his bloodstream.
So Kent knew he had to get ahead of the timeline, and since he couldn’t get his undead and other legions there due to some restriction, he had to go for the next best option.
Sword King Shawn is different. He wants to cultivate in a challenging environment, and since Kent needs someone in that world to report to him, he chose him.
Of course, he considered sending him to the tower to train in the dungeons, but in the end, he decided to send him to Fedora.
This way, he wouldn’t only grow beyond the limit of a medium world but also gain more experience by helping the Rebel Alliance handle the attackers from the Orc Alliance.
If he were to send him to the tower, his growth would stagnate at the peak of the core formation stage, since the rank of the owner determines the realm of those living there.
This means everyone inside the tower will not level up after forming their core and evolving it seven times. Of course, one could say Kent should just go to Fedora so they can keep growing.
However, the tower grows as Kent grows, and according to what Gaia told him, he must either use an Ascension platform to ascend or undergo the heavenly tribulation.

These are the only ways the limit will be broken. So Kent can find himself in an immortal world today, but the people connected to him would not continue to grow, considering they are in an immortal world.

But that is also good. The moment they reach the peak of a medium world, they can continue to grow their minds, souls, and bodies, which, from what he knew, don’t have any limitations inside or outside the tower.
So he didn’t want to limit the Sword King, whose swordsmanship is already at the peak of this world. He needed the danger to grow, and what better way to do that than to send him to a high world.
He is not linked to the tower, so he can continue to grow there. One of the many cheats the world teleporter can do. Not even the laws can stop him.
They appeared atop a mountain somewhere in Fedora. Kent quickly scanned the area to determine their location.
⟦Location: Mountain Hyib, territory of the Rabbitkin⟧
"Looks like we are in enemy territory," Kent said, and Dori nodded. But to Kent’s shock, the world teleporter in his hand beeped, and some names appeared.
⟦World: Fedora⟧
⌊ Tigerkin Territory
⌊ Rabbitkin Territory
⌊ Catkin Territory
⌊ Foxkin Territory
⌊ Hellhound Territory
⌊ Lionkin Territory
⌊ Batkin Territory
⌊ Orc Territory
This means he can use it to teleport to any territory he wants inside Fedora. "How convenient," Kent smiled and turned to Sword King Shawn.
"Welcome to Fedora, Sword King. This is how a high world feels."
"It’s indeed a wonder that I was in a medium world a second ago, and now, I am in a high world. I feel energized," Sword King Shawn said with a smile.

"Yeah, well, you needed a place to expand your Sword Realm, so this is a good enough place for that. There are many beasts here, and the danger is also more harrowing than the medium world we came from, so have fun."
"Thank you... I will benefit more here and perhaps even finally make some progress in my sword path." Sword King Shawn was ecstatic.
He found a primitive sword path while exploring the ancient battlefield of parting. He had been stuck for a while now. Hopefully, he can make progress soon.
"Let’s go before the Rabbits sense our presence," Kent teleported them away the next second. A few seconds after they were gone, a rabbit in his humanoid form appeared, wielding a large sword.
His realm was at the Spirit King stage.
"Maybe I was mistaken, but I could have sworn I sensed three people appear here," the Rabbit man said, looking around. After finding nothing, he left...
Far in the territory of the Foxkin, Kent, Sword King Shawn, and Dori appeared. However, two powerful presences descended on them a second after they appeared, causing them to turn pale.
Kent didn’t use his Rule Breaker skill to cancel the pressure simply because he could feel his bones strengthening immediately after the pressure came.
It was like the pressure was tempering his bones, something he found interesting.
Soon, two Foxkins appeared, each wielding a weapon. They were clad in battle armor and looked like they had their fair share of battles to boast about.
’Spirit Kings,’ Kent recognized their ranks.
"Who are you, and what do you want trespassing in our territory?" one of the Foxkins asked.

"I am Kent. I want to have an audience with your leader," Kent responded, only for the pressure to increase. However, before the two Foxkins could do anything, Dori walked out from behind Kent and glared at them.
"Vexen, Ralen, you two will do well to treat these two with respect."
The moment the two Foxkins’ eyes landed on Dori, who now had a ponytail and whose face now bore some green scales, they shouted, "Lady Tala..."

chapters.title: Chapter 607: Lady Tala
paragraphs: Lady Tala is a well-known name among every Foxkin living in the Emberwood Kingdom.
It’s the kingdom of the Foxkin. Unlike in Sonox, where the kingdom has many cities, Fedora has only one large city, surrounded by a wall.
Of course, they used to have smaller cities, but after the rise of the tyrant king Balma, everyone was brought into the large and well-guarded city.
Those who sided with the Orc alliance still have their smaller cities, although they also have the larger ones, where most of their powerhouses are located.
This also shows that the world of Fedora is much smaller than Sonox. However, that doesn’t make it any weaker compared to other high worlds.
Dori, who is known as Lady Tala, was what they referred to as a foreign invader in this world.
From time to time, people from other worlds come to theirs, sometimes by mistake, such as stepping into a warp in space or a damaged teleportation formation.

Since everything is within the same space and time, just a slight mistake can take a person to a different place. Of course, some come there using their own methods, just like Kent did with his World Teleporter.
Dori was once like him. However, instead of the Foxkin attacking, they took her in when she appeared. She was but a weak child, after all.

Thus, she lived in their kingdom and even became friends with Princess Lyra, the youngest princess of the Foxkins. Dori used the name Tala when she appeared in this world, so that was how she was known.

After becoming friends with Princess Lyra, she used her superior mind to help her do things that soon drew the attention of the king. Eventually, she was recognized as someone with a superior intellect, so they appointed her as an advisor.
Through her intelligence, which was mostly occupied with scheming, they made a bold move, which ultimately helped the king ascend to the stage of a Spirit Lord.
That was when her status rose from mere advisor to Supreme Advisor—Dori may have forgotten to tell Kent about that part.
But she was someone of great value to the Foxkins, so when Vexen and Ralen saw her, they immediately recognized her and quickly relieved the pressure, freeing Kent and Sword King Shawn.
"Lady Tala..." the two Foxkin shouted, looking both shocked and happy.
"No need to shout, Ralen. How is your mother, by the way?" Dori asked.
Ralen smiled and flew down, stopping when there were only a few meters between him and Dori. "My mother is doing well. She missed you, though..."
"Princess Lyra told us you had to go back to your world for a bit... everybody misses you badly."
"Well, I am back now." Dori smiled. "By the way, this is my ma—my brother Kent and Uncle Shawn."
⟪Play along, master. Telling them you are my master will certainly cause you some trouble. I’m quite a big deal here.⟫
Dori said to Kent, who smirked slightly and made sure Sword King Shawn understood the assignment. Sword King Shawn nodded.
Vexen and Ralen nodded at Kent and Uncle Shawn. "Sorry about before. We are just doing our job, and since we didn’t see Lady Tala, we had to treat you as enemies."
"Don’t worry about it..." Kent smiled. "It was a refreshing feeling."

Though he knew he had to reach the Nirvana stage in body cultivation before he could temper his bones, the feeling he got while under the pressure of the two spirit kings made him want to feel more of that.
"How bad are things these days?" Dori asked, and the two Foxkin sighed.
"It is bad, my lady. After you left, we managed to strengthen our alliance with the Tigerkin and Catkin. However, the Orcs managed to get the Hellhounds, Lionkin, Batkin, and Rabbitkin on their side.
And the worst part, they keep attacking us almost every month."
"It’s that bad, huh?" Dori turned and looked at Kent...
Kent smiled. "Let’s meet the king first; the rest will take care of itself later." Dori nodded.
"Take us to King Hkum. My brother and my uncle want to have an audience with him."
"By of course, my lady, right this way," Vexen and Ralen began leading the way.
’Looks like your rebel alliance isn’t doing too well, Lady Tala,’ Kent said through his connection with Dori, causing the Mind Weaver to blush.
⟪Don’t call me that, Master.⟫
’But I will; it suits you better,’ Kent smiled, watching Dori turn and glare at him. Sword King Shawn wondered what was happening between the two of them. However, he chose to mind his own business.
⟪But they are indeed not doing well. However, since you are here now, though the odds are too much for you to handle, knowing you, I believe you can do something to help them.⟫
’Yeah, well, Kaizo is hungry for some action, and to be frank, I also need to blow off some steam and perhaps know how much I have grown before entering seclusion.’
⟪Then that is good.⟫ Dori smiled as they moved through the forest.
Since Fedora is a world of beasts, the land is mostly forest. They have that natural way of life going on. But that doesn’t mean they don’t have a good standing when it comes to building structures.

They have towering and elegant cities with great architectural designs that can rival most human cities in Sonox. Emberwood Forest, as the Foxkin call it, is located at the center of the yellow maple leaf forest.

It’s one of the many beautiful forests in the Fedora region. Right now, Kent stood atop a mountain, looking into the distance, where a beautiful city stood mighty within the embrace of a beautiful, yellow forest.

The city is very large, and while Kent couldn’t measure it exactly, the estimated distance between them and the city is approximately 5,000 miles. But even at that vast distance, he could see a very large city rising to the sky, shining with its beauty.
"Wow, this place is beautiful." Kent couldn’t hide his admiration.
"Indeed. It is so natural," Uncle Shawn added.

This caused Vexen and Ralen to smile. Though they didn’t know Kent and Uncle Shawn, they knew they were related to Lady Tala (Dori), so hearing them praise their city was like hearing Lady Tala praise them.
Suddenly, a carriage pulled by wyverns appeared in the distance, speeding toward them...
’There are wyverns here.’ Kent raised his brow.
⟪No, Master, they are arrays... complex arrays.⟫

chapters.title: Chapter 608: Entering Emberwood
paragraphs: The carriages came from Emberwood, the city of the Foxkin, pulled by wyverns. For a moment, Kent thought the wyverns were the real deal.
However, Dori’s words shut down those thoughts, which then led him to wonder just how real arrays can be.
It just didn’t make any sense. The arrays he knew were mainly conjured into shields, formations, and other structures, not something this complex and almost tangible.
Almost real?
They are perhaps real, considering they are producing the sounds real wyverns make, and adding to that, they also have the natural reactions that a real wyvern would have.
They are basically the real deal, and Kent just couldn’t wrap his mind around it.
But when they landed—or more like when they approached them and hovered before them—he scanned them using his enchanted eyes, and the results were not what he had expected.
⟦Name: Animated Arrays (Wyvern Mounts)⟧
⟦Grade: Tier 15⟧

⟦Description: Animated Arrays drawn by Array Emperor Ashfur, one of the only three Array Emperors in Fedora. Using complex runes and symbols, he created animated beasts that act and behave like real beasts.
The Wyvern Mounts are comparable to Tier 14 True beasts.⟧
’Well, that is just classic, isn’t it, Dori?’ Kent asked, and Dori smiled.
⟪He is a rather good array master. Perhaps you should let big sister Alina intern with him for a few weeks; she might just surprise you.
After all, as an Array Emperor, he can draw between Tier 15 and 17. And in case you don’t know, one of those arrays would be enough to wipe out the entirety of Sonox.⟫
Kent didn’t say much and just watched as a Spirit Emperor, a rather handsome young man, walked out from the leading carriage, wearing a smile on his face as his eyes landed on Dori.

For some reason, Kent didn’t like that smile. It looked perverted, which begs the question: were his eyes deceiving him simply because he was overprotective of Dori, or is the bastard truly a pervert?

The answer remains unknown, but he has his eyes on the bastard. Though he can’t even think of having the means to kill him, he can always use one of his many overpowered treasures to make him regret his life decisions.
"Lady Tala, glad to see you again," the man said, his smile still in place.
’This bastard,’ Kent cursed him, but couldn’t say it out loud.
The bastard in front of him was stronger in terms of strength, cultivation, speed, and mind. Though his soul was protected, that wasn’t an open invitation to ask for a beating.
"General Raynar, glad to see you too," Dori replied before turning to Kent and Sword King Shawn. "This is my brother Kent and Uncle Shawn."
The general didn’t seem to care much about Kent and Uncle Shawn, but thanks to Dori’s importance to his people, he was forced to give a polite smile before shifting back to Dori.
Kent smirked inwardly and promised to let Kaizo punch this bastard to oblivion. Though Kent was weak, if he put his mind to it, he could kill the bastard.
After all, he had created a sword move that he couldn’t use now if he didn’t want to kill himself in the process. However, he now had a counter, even if he were to die.

Elaine now had the power of life and death, and as such, she could bring him back. So he knew he could use it at least once, and that alone was a guaranteed killing move, so the bastard could continue to act smug.
"We would like to have an audience with the king, so if you don’t mind, escort us back to the city," Dori said, and General Raynar nodded.
"Come on in," he gestured forward, calling the second carriage that came with him. "Your brother and uncle can take that one since this one is more cramped for the four of us."
Kent could see the sneer at the corner of General Raynar’s mouth, but he knew this wasn’t the time to do anything. Though he also wouldn’t want the general to have the last laugh.

"Actually, we brought our own carriage." As petty as Kent was, he wouldn’t back down when it came to the battle of who had the last laugh, so he brought out his golden carriage that immediately brightened the sky.
Though a Tier 13 array protected the carriage being offered, the golden carriage looked fancier than the ones being offered, so naturally, Kent won this one.
"You can lead the way, General Raynar," Dori said, hiding her smile. She knew what her master was doing and why it was petty; she couldn’t help liking this side of him.
General Raynar could only nod, hide the anger in his eyes, and lead the way. Kent, Dori, and Uncle Shawn took the golden carriage.
Inside, all sounds were cut off, so not even General Raynar could hear what was being said in there.
Once they were inside, Uncle Shawn smiled, "I didn’t know you were this petty, Kent."
Kent smiled and brushed his hair with his hand. "What can I say, that bastard pisses me off."
Dori and Uncle Shawn smiled, hearing that. Although he acted like a child, Kent was, to some extent, a child.

In his memories of Jest, he had only reviewed up to when he was 32 years old, and in his past life on Earth, he was in his mid-thirties. Compared to the average adult in a cultivation world, he was but a child.
A few minutes later, they entered the city’s borders, which were actually the yellow maple forest protected by the Tier 16 arrays drawn by the Array Emperor Ashfur.
Thankfully, with General Raynar leading the way, they quickly passed through and entered the polished city. It was one with grandeur.
The buildings were made of the finest wood, protected by millions of arrays and formations. Most were made purely of arrays. The air was fresh and natural.
If Earth could get this air, perhaps the average adult’s lifespan would move to 150 years. But the place was nice and clean, with thousands of houses lining the area.
From what Kent could observe, there were also stores and fancy restaurants that served better food than most of the ones he had seen in Vastport city.
"This place is nice..."
They flew toward the inner section of the city, toward the king’s palace, while attracting as much attention as possible.

"Lady Tala, glad to see you again," the man said, his smile still in place.
’This bastard,’ Kent cursed him, but couldn’t say it out loud.
The bastard in front of him was stronger in terms of strength, cultivation, speed, and mind.
Though his soul was protected, that wasn’t an open invitation to ask for a beating.
"General Raynar, glad to see you too," Dori replied before turning to Kent and Sword King Shawn.
"This is my brother Kent and Uncle Shawn."
The general didn’t seem to care much about Kent and Uncle Shawn, but thanks to Dori’s importance to his people, he was forced to give a polite smile before shifting back to Dori.
Kent smirked inwardly and promised to let Kaizo punch this bastard to oblivion.
Though Kent was weak, if he put his mind to it, he could kill the bastard.
After all, he had created a sword move that he couldn’t use now if he didn’t want to kill himself in the process.
However, he now had a counter, even if he were to die.
Elaine now had the power of life and death, and as such, she could bring him back.
So he knew he could use it at least once, and that alone was a guaranteed killing move, so the bastard could continue to act smug.
"We would like to have an audience with the king, so if you don’t mind, escort us back to the city," Dori said, and General Raynar nodded.
"Come on in," he gestured forward, calling the second carriage that came with him.
"Your brother and uncle can take that one since this one is more cramped for the four of us."
Kent could see the sneer at the corner of General Raynar’s mouth, but he knew this wasn’t the time to do anything.
Though he also wouldn’t want the general to have the last laugh.

"Actually, we brought our own carriage." As petty as Kent was, he wouldn’t back down when it came to the battle of who had the last laugh, so he brought out his golden carriage that immediately brightened the sky.
Though a Tier 13 array protected the carriage being offered, the golden carriage looked fancier than the ones being offered, so naturally, Kent won this one.
"You can lead the way, General Raynar," Dori said, hiding her smile.
She knew what her master was doing and why it was petty; she couldn’t help liking this side of him.
General Raynar could only nod, hide the anger in his eyes, and lead the way.
Kent, Dori, and Uncle Shawn took the golden carriage.
Inside, all sounds were cut off, so not even General Raynar could hear what was being said in there.
Once they were inside, Uncle Shawn smiled, "I didn’t know you were this petty, Kent."
Kent smiled and brushed his hair with his hand.
"What can I say, that bastard pisses me off."
Dori and Uncle Shawn smiled, hearing that.
Although he acted like a child, Kent was, to some extent, a child.
In his memories of Jest, he had only reviewed up to when he was 32 years old, and in his past life on Earth, he was in his mid-thirties.
Compared to the average adult in a cultivation world, he was but a child.
A few minutes later, they entered the city’s borders, which were actually the yellow maple forest protected by the Tier 16 arrays drawn by the Array Emperor Ashfur.
Thankfully, with General Raynar leading the way, they quickly passed through and entered the polished city.
It was one with grandeur.
The buildings were made of the finest wood, protected by millions of arrays and formations.
Most were made purely of arrays.
The air was fresh and natural.
If Earth could get this air, perhaps the average adult’s lifespan would move to 150 years.
But the place was nice and clean, with thousands of houses lining the area.
From what Kent could observe, there were also stores and fancy restaurants that served better food than most of the ones he had seen in Vastport city.
"This place is nice..."
They flew toward the inner section of the city, toward the king’s palace, while attracting as much attention as possible.

chapters.title: Chapter 609: Meeting King Hkum
paragraphs: After entering Emberwood, they flew for a couple of minutes before coming to a stop in front of a tall, elegant building.
It was made from the finest materials, and the arrays protecting the building were enough to withstand even a full-blown attack from a Spirit Lord.

"Open the gate, the Supreme Advisor has returned," General Raynar shouted. The large gate immediately started to open, passing through many formations. After a while, the gate fully opened, and carriages entered.
The carriage moved in, and a few seconds later, they stopped again. This time, they had to get down and walk.
The moment Kent, Dori, and Shawn alighted, a pretty young fox girl jumped into Dori’s tiny arms, sending the two of them to the ground.
"Princess Lyra, you—" Dori tried to say something, but she was on the ground before she could say anything.
Princess Lyra was just too happy to see her friend again, so she couldn’t help jumping into her arms as tears fell from her eyes.
Kent just shook his head and looked forward.
His eyes landed on three individuals. Two of them were men, and the third was a lady. All three looked like royalty.
However, while Kent saw many foxkins with fur on their bodies and faces while riding through the streets of Emberwood, these three were more human-like, like General Ragnar.
The only things that showed they were foxkins were their tails and pointed, fluffy ears. Aside from that, they were basically human like him.
The two men with the lady each had green hair, green fluffy ears, and four tails—well, one of them had five tails, though the fifth tail was still at the blooming stage.
As for the lady, she had white hair with six fluffy tails.
In the fox race, their tails show their power.
The higher the number of tails, the more powerful they are, so this was a clear sign that the lady was much stronger than the two handsome men standing on the left and right.
Watching their younger sister now dusting off Dori’s clothes, they couldn’t help but hide their embarrassed expressions.
"Sorry, Lady Tala, I was just too happy to see you," Princess Lyra said, smiling embarrassedly.
"Don’t worry about it. Also, I already told you to call me Tala; we are friends," Dori said with a smile before focusing on the three individuals.
"Princess Arien, good to see you again," Dori said. "Prince Sylas, Prince Daryn."
"Glad to see you again, Lady Tala," all three said. Dori turned and introduced Kent and Sword King Shawn. Princess Arien and her two brothers nodded in response to Kent and Sword King Shawn.
"Thank you for saving us the last time," Princess Lyra said, causing her siblings to raise their brows.
"You are the mysterious foreigner who saved the princess?" General Raynar asked, taken aback by the sudden reveal she had been hoping to know for months now.
Though Nyxira wiped the memories of most of the beastkins they saved when rescuing Dori, Dori made sure Princess Lyra’s and her maid’s memories weren’t wiped.
So she told her family, which included the general. According to her, the people who saved them are some of the most powerful beings she has ever seen.
She was just a naive Level 3 Great Sage then, so when she saw the colossal beasts that Kent and his team killed that day, she couldn’t help singing their praises to her family.

To her siblings and those who knew how she was rescued, it seemed that perhaps some powerful beings, who could bring their race to its knees, had come for Dori. But hearing it was the weak Level 2 Sovereign human before them who saved her, the general couldn’t help but ask.
"Well, they weren’t that difficult to kill." Kent, of course, wouldn’t tell them the strength level of the bandits they killed that day.
Though this is a High world, it doesn’t mean everyone’s strength is between the Spirit Ascension and Heavenly Ascension stages. Some people are still at the Root Master stage.

The only difference is that the limit on them doesn’t stop them at the Core Formation stage. They can rise as far as the Heavenly Ascension stage before they will be required to ascend to an immortal world.
General Raynar studied Kent’s demeanor for a few seconds before a sign escaped his lips. "Thank you for saving the princess and the Supreme Advisor."
"Don’t worry about it. I wouldn’t sleep well knowing this spoiled brat runs off getting herself caught," Kent said, roughing Dori’s hair.
"Hey, who said we were caught? It was a calculated move that allowed us to maintain our cover and drew suspicion away," Dori said, puffing her cheeks.
"Yeah... yeah... I guess next time, include the possibility of getting caught in your calculation."
"You—" Dori turned away from Kent, folding her small hands on her chest, puffing her cheeks like a spoiled loli.

The princesses and princes watching this couldn’t help but wonder just where their respected and elegant Supreme Advisor had gone. In the end, they just smiled and led the way inside, where the king was waiting for them.
He was already aware of the Supreme Advisor’s arrival the moment two guards, Ralen and Vexen, stopped Kent, Dori, and Sword King Shawn.
When it comes to space magic, the foxkin are the best in that field. So sending a message to their king thousands of miles away wasn’t much of a stress.

They entered a large hall where six people could be seen sitting in what looked like a meeting. The setup showed that the muscular man with pointed fox ears and eight fluffy black tails was King Hkum.
He was seated in the head chair, a throne-like chair made from pure gold. On his left sat three people, and on his right were two.
All five with him are at the 9th level Spirit Emperor stage, while the king is at the level 4 Spirit Lord stage.
"Father, look who is back!" Princess Lyra, who was walking with Dori, said, holding Dori’s small hand. She was happy that her best friend had returned.
"I am not blind, Little Lyra..." King Hkum said with a smile, and the five people inside the hall with him also smiled. They all seemed happy to see their Supreme Advisor return safely.
"Welcome back to Emberwood, Lady Tala. It’s good to see you well and in one piece," King Hkum said, and Dori nodded.
"It’s good to be back, too."
They quickly sat down after Dori introduced Kent and Sword King Shawn.

chapters.title: Chapter 610: He is Poisoned
paragraphs: "It’s good to finally see family members of our one and only Supreme Advisor. Though we don’t know each other yet, I have a feeling that, as someone related to Lady Tala, you are also great thinkers," King Hkum said, smiling at Kent and Sword King Shawn.
Kent smiled and shook his head. "We try to keep up with her, but I doubt we will ever rise to her level."
The king and the five there laughed.
Though Dori didn’t say much about what she did for the Foxkin and the rebel alliance, she had indeed been invaluable to them.

She not only helped the king obtain something that enabled him to advance his cultivation base to the Spirit Lord stage, but she also assisted others in raising their cultivation bases by utilizing her superior mental and analytical thinking abilities.

Well, she was merely using what she could to avoid causing more harm to the Foxkins. If she were to unleash her full mind, the battle would end within an hour, but that would cause more harm to the Foxkins.
But even her tamed mind was enough to earn her the respect of those around her.
"I guess we are fortunate to have her as one of our advisors," Elder Joren, a green-haired man with eight tails, said, and the others nodded.
"How was your trip then? Princess Lyra told us you said you would be going away for a while, so I hoped everything worked out well," King Hkum asked.
"Yes. I finally managed to reconnect with my family. However, my brother wants to see you and have a discussion with you all, so here we are," Dori responded.
She knew they wouldn’t want her to leave again, so she made sure they understood the reason she returned was because of Kent and that they should pay attention to him.
"However, before that, Vexen told me things hadn’t been good lately. Care to give me a rundown on what has been going on since I left?"
Hearing her words, the king, his elders, princesses, and princes sighed. King Hkum looked at his elders and sighed even harder.
"To be frank, after you left, we didn’t have much of a problem until two months ago, when those Hellhound dogs started looking for trouble with us.
They would, from time to time, attack our borders. A couple of our men guarding the borders died, and some were even taken away.
We tried to retrieve them, but since the Batkins share borders with the Hellhounds and are all on the side of the Tyrant King, we couldn’t have much success.
"We even lost more men in the last operation. So that is what has been going on."
"Sounds bad. How about our allies, the Tigerkins and Catkins? Why didn’t they send their men to help you?" Dori sighed and then asked.
"The Tigerkins are also clashing with the Lionkins, and the Catkins are holding their own against the Rabbitkins.
I think that Orc bastard—excuse my words—wants to make a move on us. Though they are still treating our three races as defiers, they don’t yet know we are in an alliance.
So we also didn’t want to show ourselves yet until King Ralyk and Queen Seris manage to break into the Spirit Lord stage.
But I can’t shake the feeling that King Balma is making a move soon," King Hkum said, and Kent couldn’t help laughing.
"That bastard is probably hiding somewhere dark, tending to the poison in his body. I don’t think you should worry about him coming or taking action for another six to eight years."
"What?" the king and his people shouted, hearing Kent’s words.
"My brother is right. King Balma won’t be taking action anytime soon," Dori added to Kent’s words.
"And why is that?" Elder Nexen asked, confused as to why their supreme leader and her brother could say such a thing.
"That is because I poisoned him the last time I came to rescue my sister," Kent revealed, showing where his confidence was coming from, causing the king and the elders to gasp at such bold claims.
Their eyes showed their disbelief.
"He is telling the truth. I witnessed it with my own eyes," Dori added with a smile.
"How is that even possible? I mean, not that I want to look down on you, but a mere Sovereign had no business looking even a Spirit Lord in the eye, much less fighting one... It’s just—"
"Unbelievable," Kent smiled. "I know, but for the record, I was a Great Sage back then when I gave that bastard the middle finger."
"What is a middle finger?" Princess Lyra asked innocently.
"It’s nothing, princess..." Dori glared at Kent and smiled weakly.
Kent smirked and looked at the king. "No need to think too much about it. The poison I gave that bastard is enough to keep him away from all fights for a long time.
However, I think he asked his allies to keep attacking you to divert suspicion away from the fact that he is no longer capable of fighting.
But don’t worry too much about it. I will help handle them for you."
Kent’s words were bold and arrogant, yet knowing he was the brother of their supreme advisor, they couldn’t help but feel that they could trust him.
"Pardon my words, but how can a mere Sovereign help us?" Prince Daryn asked, not sounding arrogant, yet his words carried a hint of anger.
Kent knew they wouldn’t trust him easily, despite being Dori’s brother. However, he wasn’t overly concerned about whether they believed him.
His declaration to help them may sound noble, but his endgame was personal gain.
Right now, he has twelve powerful immortals who have regressed to the Root Sovereign stage, and to help them, he needs loads of Tower points.
So, what is the best way to do that if not killing loads of beasts and at the same time checking how far his legions can push their limits?

The main mission to save Planet Dusk and its people still has two years before it will be too late. But knowing the danger waiting for him there, he first wanted to raise the strength level of his legion, and that can be done using Tower points and beast bodies.
So, he wants to upgrade the dungeons at least first, and then, using the bodies collected, he will create the eight more undead he was left to create while upgrading Kaizo and the rest.
A few Spirit Ascension or Spirit King bodies will do the trick.
’I mean, one spirit Ascension Beast is worth 5 million tower points...I can’t let this golden opportunity slip through my fingers.’

chapters.title: Chapter 611: The Request
paragraphs: "To be honest with you all, I asked Tala to bring me here for two reasons.

First, my uncle here is a Sword King with unlimited potential, and while I would love to say he has no equal in my world, I have seen enough to know that even with his cultivation base, he can be an asset to your cause.
I brought him here to ask if you can take him in. Don’t worry; he won’t need your resources to grow; he already has his own.
The second is that I want to personally lead my own team against one of the beasts allied with the Orcs.
That bastard may have been poisoned now, but the moment he gets the poison out, he will come after you all to finally get you under his control.
However, I want to use his absence to create so much chaos that when he is out, it will take him some time to put his alliance back on track.

Trust me, if I were you, I wouldn’t want to be clashing with them if they have such a being on their side, but seeing they don’t have much backbone now, give me the chance to ensure they think ten times before attacking your people... for the next couple of years to come."
Kent didn’t know where the confidence was coming from, but for some reason, he wanted to go against odds so far greater than him that even people in High Worlds would fear.

Perhaps this was a result of his fabricated memories of his life as a god he received while awakening Zaila’s True Name, or the fact that with the attribute points left to allocate, he would be approaching the maximization threshold for the next limit to be broken.
The moment he added the point, the limit would appear.
While he knew this time the tower would suggest what he had to do to break it, he also knew that the moment the limit was broken, nobody in Sonox would be able to stand as his equal.
These limits he is breaking are much more valuable than anything he will ever gain to increase his strength. Kent’s confidence is just too great because he wants to test his strength.
So he wanted something dangerous to test himself, his legion, and his wives.
"I think you should let him, King Hkum. Although he may not appear to be it, he is actually very powerful. In your eyes, he may be just a level 2 Sovereign, but he has already broken a limit."
The moment Dori said those words, everyone’s eyes in the hall widened, except Sword King Shawn, Kent, and Dori, who spoke those words.

The people in the hall were aware of these limits. It’s the same thing that helped King Hkum take such a leap in his cultivation. It is also one of the requirements before a person can become a Spirit Lord.

Basically, most gods hadn’t yet broken three limits because, from Tier One, which is the beginning of cultivation to godhood, only two realms require one to break a limit before they can ascend to the next level.
One of these realms is the Spirit Lord realm. Aside from that, the Root Immortal stage also requires a limit to be broken first.
There are many ways to reach these limits. However, they are all challenging, and even if you achieve one, the chances of successfully breaking said limits are something nobody can easily handle.
So, for a mere Sovereign to have already broken a limit is just something very shocking.
And because of what Dori said, the King, his elders, and his children started to look at Kent differently.
"It wasn’t just him; my uncle has even reached the limit, but he doesn’t know it yet." Dori turned to Sword King Shawn.
"The reason why you are stuck at the pinnacle of the Sword King stage is because you have reached a limit which seems to have something to do with your imagination.

To progress, take your time and break your sword realm down to the basic stage, to the stage where everything started. Build it back up, and I assure you, by the time you are done, you will become a Sword Emperor."
Yet again, the king and his people became puzzled. They just didn’t understand where these two monsters came from.
It would be fine, though shocking, if only Kent had such potential, but for Sword King Shawn to be this monstrous too, it put things into perspective for them.
They started to wonder just how many Kents were out there.
If only they knew he had loads of them inside his tower, with potential that many would kill to have even a fraction of.
"This is a delicate request, so give us some time to deliberate on it, and we will get back to you. However, regarding your uncle living here, he is welcome to stay for as long as he wants.

This showed progress.
"Thanks for accepting my request, King Hkum. I am grateful." Kent was indeed grateful. But while Kent was indeed grateful, the Foxkins are the same, for they are aware of what swordsmen can do.
One thing about swordsmen is that they can grow endlessly regardless of their cultivation base, so they wouldn’t let go of such an asset.
Hearing he would soon be breaking his limit, they wouldn’t want to lose him, not when they are going against an alliance of five powerful Beast factions.
The odds were far greater than something they could handle, so they would spend most of their efforts ensuring that someone who would soon break a limit on themselves was well cared for.

"Arien, take Lady Tala and his family to her residence. Of course, you can follow them too, Lyra," King Hkum said, and the white-haired princess nodded. Her little sister was even happier to hear what their father said.
She is free to play with her best friend again.
Princess Arien led Dori, Kent, and Sword King Shawn away toward a small yet fancy building that, by a count, Kent knew had enough room for everyone.

Kent couldn’t help smiling slightly as he watched her six fluffy white tails move and contract whenever her confidence level dropped.

Unlike her little sister Princess Lyra, who was busily chatting with Sword King Shawn and Dori, she seemed more shy... Not that it was unexpected. After all, she had no friends besides her little sister and brothers.
Life of a princess...especially one that is surrounded by war.
"I know I am handsome, but to make a whole princess speechless, I think I should probably compete in the next Universe’s Most Handsome,"
Kent said with a smile, causing the shy princess to trip over a stone. However, before she could fall flat on her face, Prince Charming was waiting with his arms open for her to fall into.

I brought him here to ask if you can take him in.
Don’t worry; he won’t need your resources to grow; he already has his own.
The second is that I want to personally lead my own team against one of the beasts allied with the Orcs.
