chapters.title: Chapter 623: The Creator of Chaos (8) [Bonus]
paragraphs: When Kent was assigning tasks to his legion, he excluded Skoggr, Gorzak, and Kazarak simply because he had a different mission for them.
Both Skoggr and Gorzak are orcs, and Kazarak is a lionkin who can summon Hellhounds. This shows they are not welcome in the Foxkin race.
Although the king and his elders accepted them, Kent knew their hatred would forever make them wary of these three subordinates of his.
That was when the idea clicked.
What if, before he leaves Fedora, he made sure the Lionkin and the Hellhounds became enemies, and perhaps lowered the trust the Lionkin had in the orc alliance?
It sounded like the perfect plan, so Kent devised a plan to utilize Skoggr, Gorzak, and Kazarak for it.
"Master, from the map you gave, this is their strongest army base. If we attack here, it will result in the effect we want," Skoggr said when Kent appeared.

"Indeed. However, I have no doubt there are more than two Spirit Emperors there and perhaps hundreds of Spirit Kings. The only good part is that there are no children, so we can go all out," Kent smiled.
"Will you also be joining us?" Gorzak asked, and Kent nodded.
"Indeed. However, we all have to attack only once. This means only use your strongest moves. The aim is to kill as many as we can using just one attack. The rest will take care of itself."
The three nodded.

"Kazarak, like we discussed, summon the five strongest Hellhounds that, when they detonate their core, the destruction will be massive. And don’t worry, they will respawn back inside the dungeon, so go all out.
The base is big, so summon them at random places, but keep the interval vast so the destruction will cover a much wider area."

"So, who will go first, and how are we going to enter without alerting the Spirit Emperors and Kings?" Skoggr asked, ready to handle the mission, considering it was his first since becoming Kent’s subordinate.
Kent retrieved three talismans from the tower storage and handed them to them. "Skoggr, you will go first, after that Gorzak will go, then Kazarak.
This talisman will teleport you to wherever you can see in that base. Remember, the moment you attack, enter the tower."
They nodded. "In that case, let’s get the party on the road," Kent smiled.
Skoggr pointed at the eastern part of the base. "I will attack there."
"Then I will go to the west." Gorzak also picked his spot, and Kazarak chose the center where he could spread out his five summons.
"Here I go then." Skoggr took out his large Great Axe and channeled his energy into it. Using the talisman, he vanished and appeared at the eastern part of the military base of the Lionkin.

The Lionkin soldiers were about their business, planning when they would attack the Tigerkin next, when suddenly an orc appeared in the air and, without any warning, a large 50-meter-long Great Axe burning with red flames shot from the clouds, shaking the very ground they stood on.

"The Orc King sends his regards." Skoggr’s voice filled the space as the axe fell on the ground, destroying everything in its path. The shockwave was wild as it swept through the entire area, killing those it could.
The Sovereign and Core formation experts were burned to ash, and even the spirit Ascension and Spirit Kings didn’t do much better. Most died, including a few Spirit Kings..
"The Hellhounds were right, you guys are traitors."
Suddenly, at the western side, a mocking voice filled the space as a 70-meter hammer descended from the clouds.
Although it wasn’t on fire, the Sovereigns and Core formation experts within the western region were crushed to death even before the hammer fell.
Gorzak’s Earthsplitter Hammer has an enchanted ability that makes it several times heavier.
This means that with the skill that had already turned the hammer into a 70-meter-long monstrosity, the enchantment made the whole thing worse.
Hundreds died, and Gorzak vanished the next second before a Spirit Emperor could lock onto him. If that had happened, he wouldn’t have been able to vanish back into the tower.

But before they could process what had happened, their third nightmare arrived. Kazarak appeared for less than a second, but in his place, five 40-meter-tall Hellhounds appeared 2 km apart and detonated their cores.

For creatures that are natural fire users, their detonation was devastating. The entire landscape was burned, and everything in the path of the explosion was reduced to ashes, charred bodies, and severely injured lions.

But their pain didn’t end there. Just when the Hellhounds detonated, five powerful sword lights came from the distance, exactly 10 km away, and long before they reached them, those in the path of these sword arcs were already quaking in their boots.
Kent, who had been standing 10 km away, watched as three Spirit Emperors, just as he had predicted, appeared and, using their strongest defense, blocked three of the attacks.
However, two found their way to the military base, cutting a large crater into the ground. Those in the path of these two attacks died.
The Spirit Emperors managed to defend against the three Void Cleaves, but they sustained some injuries.
Kent didn’t let them see him, so he vanished before they could sense him, but he made sure they knew what had happened here.
"Traitors, I knew the Hellhounds were telling the truth. Lord Balma will hear of this." Those words made the Lionkin very angry, so they immediately contacted their king.
Though they couldn’t see the last attack, they knew someone who could injure even a spirit Emperor was no easy person, meaning what he said wasn’t a lie.

That meant the Hellhounds were indeed behind the attack. Seeing two orcs, a Lionkin, and five Hellhounds that even employed suicide moves, the evidence pointed to the Hellhounds, and as such, revenge was in order.
Kent left them in a state of destruction and beyond repair. They lost thousands of soldiers, and that was precisely what Kent was after.
By the time he returned to the Hound Barracks, the battle was over.
The outcome of these two coordinated attacks will soon be revealed...

chapters.title: Chapter 624: The Aftermath of Chaos [Bonus]
paragraphs: Coincidences are indeed a thing.
It had already been two days since Kent led his legion and his Dragon Harem to evade the Hound Barracks and kill every last Hellhound. Not even one managed to escape.
Their loss was brutal, and as such, when the Hound King found out, he was so enraged that he nearly burned down his palace.
However, that anger was soon directed at the Lionkin. The reason being that every last Hellhound died, and they didn’t know something that grim had happened.
A day after the attack, a unit of Hellhounds, who were scheduled to replace another unit, discovered the attack and immediately alerted their king.
The coincidence part was that a few hours after the Hellhounds became aware of this massacre, the Lions attacked one of their other barracks.
Perhaps, sometimes, the anger most people feel should be resolved first before battles.

The Lion King wasn’t any different from The Hellhound King. When news reached him that the Hellhounds colluded with the Orcs to attack them, he knew the Orcs couldn’t be touched, so all his anger was directed at the Hellhounds.
He ordered a full-blown war, and so, a day later—which was a few hours after the Hellhounds received news of the massacre of their soldiers—the Lionkin arrived, and the battle was cataclysmic.

Thousands died in their first clash, and despite having the option to talk, none believed the other. So, a day later, the second clash occurred, and that was what had been happening since Kent’s mission.
The man in question was currently sleeping in the house given to them by the Foxkin.
His ladies were somewhere in the city, spending time there while Kent waited for the limit to break.
Meanwhile, the Foxkin, who were keeping tabs on the war between the Lionkin and Hellhounds, were so shocked that they didn’t know what to do.

It was just too shocking. Kent hadn’t even told them he had such a plan up his sleeve. He only told them after the mission. And so now that they were seeing the outcome, they just didn’t know what to say.
Currently, inside the palace, King Hkum, his elders, and Queen Amorian were meeting with Dori to understand something.
"Lady Tala, what is your take on what is going on now?" King Hkum asked.
Dori smiled, hearing his question. What her master did was indeed something worth admiring, and now she was left to make them understand the kind of person Kent was...
"Big brother Kent only did what he did, so you can have a moment of peace for perhaps a few years to come. He knew that with the Orc king poisoned, the four who allied with them would be weakened.
This was why he ensured that two of them fought and killed each other. And knowing the Hellhounds, they won’t stop anytime soon. So this leaves us with the most pressing question:
Would the Orcs retaliate?

The answer is no, they won’t. They are currently leaderless. Their king is poisoned, and as a result, they wouldn’t want to engage in any major battles. This means we now have some years to observe things.
The Lionkin is the third strongest in the Orc Alliance, but with how ferocious the Hellhounds are, they will lose more men.
When that happens, they will become useless to King Balma. By then, he will only have the Batkin and the Rabbitkin on his side. That will make it three against three.
However, I have reasons to believe that odd will be useless when the time comes."
"Oh, and why is that?" Elder Joren asked. He could sense some confidence in Dori’s words that made him wonder just where it was coming from.

By the time the Orc King comes out of seclusion, you will be ready to bring him to his knees with just your pinky."

’I mean, she is not wrong. I would indeed have the power to bring him to his knees with my pinky. Even now, I can go toe-to-toe with a peak Spirit Emperor.
What then would become of me after I come out of seclusion?’ Kent mused.
"Alright, let’s do it."

chapters.title: Chapter 625: Midnight Shadows [Bonus]
paragraphs: Guardianship!
That was one of the many towers Kent had in his overpowered Tower system. It allowed him to become the protector of anyone he chose.
The time he awakened the guardian tower was when he became Li Hua’s guardian, after he found her grandma half-dead in the woods. Since then, he hadn’t added anyone to the Guardian Tower.
However, now, he was on the verge of adding a race close to a million foxkins that were more powerful than anyone could even imagine.
The responsibility was huge, but Kent didn’t even want to start imagining what would happen when he became their guardian.
"Becoming the guardian of an entire race, huh? I wonder what will be required of me then." Kent had to spend a day getting accustomed to his strength before meeting the king and his subjects.
Queen Amorian, the two princesses, and the two princes were also there. But aside from them, Array Emperor Ashfur was also present.
He was surprisingly much older than everyone there, or more like he looked much older than everyone there.
Some immortals looked no older than 20, so it was normal for him to be much younger than the king but appear older than him.
However, in this instance, Array Emperor Ashfur was actually much older than King Hkum and the five elders. This raised questions about his age.
Kent, of course, had to look, considering he felt some form of danger from the old man when their gazes met. So he checked, and what he saw made him wonder many things inwardly.
⟦Name: Ashfur Blinton⟧
⟦Class: Array Emperor⟧
⟦Rank: Spirit Emperor (Lvl 7)⟧
⟦Secondary Class: Shadowblade⟧
’He is an assassin, and judging by the feeling I am getting, he is one terrifying assassin.’ Kent was taken aback, but he didn’t do much to draw his attention to himself.
Of course, that didn’t mean he had to wipe the information he managed to extract without making it look extreme.
However, the last line of information he received was rather unsettling, prompting him to question who exactly the man sitting across from him was.
⟦Affiliation: Member of the Midnight Shadows⟧
He knew the man before him was dangerous. But since they were on the same side, or so it seemed, he had to appear friendly and make sure he didn’t make it look too obvious.

"Kent, this is Array Emperor Ashfur. He is responsible for every last array you see around this city. If not for his heaven-defying creations, we would have lost this city long ago," King Hkum said, introducing the mysterious Shadowblade, who held a calm smile on his face.
"Pleasure meeting you, Array Emperor. I was blown away when I saw the wyvern when I first got here..." Kent said with a polite smile.
Array Emperor Ashfur smiled. "You can just call me Sir Ashfur, and I’m glad to hear the brother of our Supreme Advisor likes my creations. I am honored."
’And that is the hook right there. This man is dangerous...’ Kent smiled, putting on a happy expression.
"If I have time, I will come around to see if I can learn a thing or two from you... I happen to have a thing for arrays and formations."
Sir Ashfur smiled and then responded, "I will be glad to have you at my shop."
The king and his subjects smiled, watching Kent and Sir Ashfur get along. It didn’t take long for Queen Amorian to change the subject.
"So, Kent, we have to favor asking. I know we don’t know each other very well, but per the direction of our Supreme Advisor, we couldn’t help but ask if you would like to become our Guardian.
I know it is a lot to ask, but we saw what you can do, and due to that, though we are asking too much, we want to ask of you this..."
Kent nodded, hearing her words. It was indeed true that if you want something done well, a lady is the right choice to lead.
Her words showed she was still skeptical about what Dori asked them to do, but she also saw what Kent could do; as such, she knew there was something more to this.
Kent knew that they were skeptical about many things, so he wanted to ensure they were all on the same page.
"To be frank, I don’t have to be your guardian to help you, and trust me, you wouldn’t have to pay a dime for me to become your guardian.
However, asking me to become your guardian will require me to make difficult decisions, such as migrating everyone when the danger is too great to bear.
Although I don’t see that happening.
But aside from that, I will also have to implement my security measures because trust me, when I become your guardian, I will be bound to you all, and that bond makes me responsible for everyone.
And as a guardian, I can’t allow even a single one of you to come to any harm. Therefore, I will implement some extreme security measures, which I believe are for the best.
So before we get down to the big question, I want to ask: do you trust me enough to give me this much privilege over your people?"
The king and his people entered a brief contemplation. What they were asking of Kent was indeed something that would make him someone akin to a god.
They would depend on him, and he would be responsible for ensuring their protection. As a guardian, he must ensure all those he is looking after are safe.
He didn’t know what would happen if he couldn’t protect them, but it was also something he wasn’t ready to handle.
Meanwhile, while the king and his people were thinking for a moment, Vexthra reached out to Kent.

’Kent, I think the person who is affiliated with the Midnight Shadows can be trusted. The Midnight Shadows is a righteous assassin organization scattered across High Worlds, Immortal, God, Supreme, and even Celestial Worlds.
They are said to be loyal followers of a once-renowned lethal assassin who was only known by his code name. Many don’t even know if he was a he or she, but he went by the codename Faceless Assassin.’
Kent’s brow raised...

chapters.title: Chapter 626: Guardianship and Rewards [Bonus]
paragraphs: ’The faceless assassin, huh?’
Kent was both amused and a little taken aback by the audacity of this claim. The faceless assassin was one of his past lives. He had already received a memory key to start retrieving those memories.
But who would have thought he would find a follower of his in this world?
’Talk about a small world... well, more like a small universe. But who would have thought a follower who believes in the Faceless Assassin, one of my past lives, would be sitting across from me?’
Kent looked at Sir Ashfur, who was conversing with King Hkum, and a smile appeared on his lips, but it vanished the next second, as the king and his people seemed to have come to a conclusion.
[Thanks, Vex, see you later.]
Kent said to Vexthra before focusing back on the king and his people. Again, Queen Amorian was the one to speak.
"We only have one question, and an honest answer would be great."
Kent nodded. "Ask away, Queen Amorian."
She also nodded and asked the sole question they all wanted answers to. "Would this guardianship affect my people in any way that would be bad for them?"
Kent smiled and answered, "As far as I am aware, aside from me becoming a guardian, that must ensure everyone is safe. Everyone will be safe from all forms of harm.
So be assured, they will be safe and happy."
Everyone nodded.

So far, they would trust their supreme advisor and take Kent as their guardian. If they ended up in bed with the devil, then they would only pray that this devil is better than the Tyrant King of the Orcs, King Balma.
Kent smiled, noting their accepting expressions.
"In that case, I will only ask once..." They looked at him as if he were some kind of guardian sent from the heavens. "Do you all want me to become your guardian?"
There was a pause. Then, they nodded, "We do."
Kent smiled, and then, as he expected, a message appeared before his view.
⟦Do you want to become the guardian of the Grayvine Foxkin?⟧
"Yes," Kent answered, and then dozens of messages started to appear. He focused on one that appeared in red because he knew it was urgent.
⟦Tower Request: How do you want to receive your gains from the Grayvine Foxkin?⟧
↠ Spiritual Qi
↠ Soul Essence
’I didn’t know why this was now optional, but I think I will go for Soul Essence simply because I have a nagging feeling I will be needing more of that in the years to come.’
When he became a Tier 13 soul cultivator, he received the option to save soul essence, which in this case would be like tower points he could later use to raise his soul cultivation.
He didn’t know why it had become like that, but a nagging feeling kept telling him it had something to do with his yet-to-awaken soul path.
So, if that was the case, he wouldn’t hesitate to store more of it. Now, he would not only receive it from killing, but the Grayvine Foxkin race would become his source of soul essence.
This made him wonder just what would become of him when he awakened his soul cultivation path.

"I don’t know what happened, but I feel like I can depend on you, Brother Kent." Just as Kent was quickly checking through the messages, Princess Lyra said this, causing her family to look at Kent strangely.
They can all feel what she felt.
Kent turned and looked at them, and he smiled. "Anyways, as your official guardian, my first order of business is..."
He looked at them with a smile that held many meanings. However, while their hearts raced, they thought he would say something outrageous, but what he said instead left their jaws hanging.
Kent took out a golden fruit from his space ring. The moment everyone’s eyes landed on the fruit, a sense of attraction dawned on them.
"This is an Immortal-grade Ambrosia apple. When consumed, it will raise the grade of your spirit roots to the Immortal grade.
In other words, if you consume this fruit, you will be able to break both the first and second limits easily." Kent laughed and threw the fruit at Sir Ashfur. "You can examine it if you want."
Hearing he was a follower of his, Kent didn’t want to even think suspiciously of him again. And now that he had become their guardian, he would know if someone was plotting against the Foxkins.

Since he couldn’t sense any ill intent from him, he trusted that he would give sound judgment. As expected, after five minutes, he looked at Kent and smiled, though a shocked expression was on his face.
"This is indeed an Ambrosia fruit, and judging by its color, it is indeed Immortal grade." The king, the elders, Queen Amorian, and her children looked at Kent in shock.

The brat who liked the attention retrieved a pouch and made it float toward the king. "Inside are 100 Immortal-grade Ambrosia apples. Take one each and pick your most trusted men and share it among them.
I don’t really care how you share it, but make sure they are trusted to the point they won’t question anything you ask them to do."
King Hkum nodded, feeling his heartbeat rise and fall. He wasn’t the only one; they were all shocked beyond their understanding.
Never in their wildest dreams did they think they would be getting the means to break their limits this easily. It was just never in their books.
"Also, Sir Ashfur, this is a Tier 17 defense and attack array. It will be challenging and time-consuming to set up, but I trust you will be able to complete it.

The moment this is set up, not even King Balma can break it. And when you use it to attack, the spirit Emperors will run from it. Even Spirit Lords will be wary." Kent again threw a scroll to Sir Ashfur and stood up.
"I will be off now. If anything, talk to Tala; she will attend to your needs." Kent walked away, teleporting into the tower the moment he was outside.
He was so excited to see his gains that he immediately opened the messages. When his eyes landed on the first two messages, his smile bloomed.
⟦Congratulations, you are now the guardian of the Grayvine Foxkin.⟧
⟦New Guardian Tools unlocked in the Guardian Tower⟧

He was so excited to see his gains that he immediately opened the messages.
When his eyes landed on the first two messages, his smile bloomed.
⟦Congratulations, you are now the guardian of the Grayvine Foxkin.⟧
⟦New Guardian Tools unlocked in the Guardian Tower⟧

chapters.title: Chapter 627: The Rewards [Bonus]
paragraphs: ⟦Congratulations, you are now the guardian of the Grayvine Foxkin.⟧
⟦New Guardian Tools unlocked in the Guardian Tower⟧
These two messages made Kent smile. This was confirmation that he had indeed added a new race to his Guardian Tower.

The first was expected, but the second was something he never expected. This was because, up until today, the only two tools he had in the Guardian Tower were the Shadow Spider he used to spy on and kill Bright Faywood.
The other was the Battle Dolls, which, from what he knew so far, would one day become the 14 lost knights. This made him wonder just what had been added now.
But aside from that, he was just happy he had added the Foxkin to his Guardian Tower because the rewards were immeasurable.

He moved on to some of the messages, which mostly discussed the responsibilities he had to fulfill as the guardian of an entire race. He had seen most of those already when he added Li Hua several months back.
But aside from that, he received some rewards, which included the Immortal Grade Ambrosia apple he gave them and the Tier 17 schematics for the array he gave to Sir Ashfur.
The tower seemed to know what he needed at the moment as a guardian and provided just that. That showed he had indeed become the guardian of an entire race.
However, there was more: the reward he would receive from the Grayvine Foxkin race. He had chosen to receive soul essence, and so far, he had something to brag about.
⟦Soul Essence: 1,270,000,600⟧

The soul essence Kent had in reserve was already enough to take him from Tier 13 to Tier 16 in soul cultivation if he wanted. However, Kent didn’t even think about doing that; he knew storing the soul essence would come in handy soon.
Having billions of soul essence was also good, but knowing why he was storing it, he could only wait to see what he could create.
Kent didn’t want to say it, but he had already started to wonder just what type of Soul Path was waiting for him to traverse.
But if the tower had already begun storing soul essence for him, then he could only wait and see what amazing path awaited him.
"Now, back to the Guardian Tools." Kent turned to the tools. He wanted to see if his next batch of tools would be enough to protect the Foxkin if need be.
He quickly accessed the message, and to his shock, the new additions were just two, but each was a powerful tool that he could use.
The first was a 3-meter-tall metallic being. It was like Veydris, but this one was much bigger, muscular, and wielded two deadly blades.
One of the swords seemed to hover behind him while he held on to another. It was clear that he was a skilled swordsman; the sword behind him seemed to act like a spirit weapon.
This made Kent wonder what this swordsman was made of or what went into making such a fighter. The second has the same design, but it was an archer.
⟦Name: Guardian Swordsman⟧
⟦Grade: Tier 14⟧
⟦Rank: SSS⟧
⟦Description: An impeccable swordsman meant to help the guardian in protecting his flocks.⟧
⟦Note: If this guardian’s tool is used in a Medium world, the rank will regress to Tier 12. The grade and rank are upgradable.⟧
⟦Price: 50,000,000 Tower Points⟧
⟦Name: Guardian Archer⟧
⟦Grade: Tier 14⟧
⟦Rank: SSS⟧
⟦Description: An impeccable archer meant to help the guardian in protecting his flocks.⟧
⟦Note: If this guardian’s tool is used in a Medium world, the rank will regress to Tier 12. The grade and rank are upgradable.⟧
⟦Price: 50,000,000 Tower Points⟧
"Interesting. To think I will be getting two powerful tools that are comparable to a Spirit King right off the bat. However, the price is a little too much. But I can handle it." Kent smiled.
He didn’t know if this was something he could really focus on to guard the Grayvine Foxkin, but he knew having five of each would put up a good fight.

The best part was that they were SSS rank, which made them comparable to someone who had broken a limit. And while Kent knew they were less likely to lose to a peak Emperor, he knew they would struggle against a Spirit Lord.
However, there was something here that made them dangerous, and that was the fact that they wouldn’t tire. In combat, unless they were destroyed, they would never get tired.
That was enough to show they were meant to guard those he truly wanted to.
"So far, I only have one of each as a gift from the tower for adding an entire race to the tower. This means I can only station these two for now.
However, considering I have billions in tower points, I can go ahead and buy a few more.
I will be entering seclusion, and judging by the number of things I need to accomplish, I don’t know how long I will be gone for, so it is better to have a backup plan."
Kent nodded. With what he had saved up, he knew the chances of his staying in seclusion for years were likely.

Thankfully, time in the tower is much faster than outside, so he knew only a couple of months would pass on the outside, but that still didn’t change the fact that he needed to ensure they were safe while he was away.
"Tower, I will purchase four of each."

His tower points were deducted, and eight Guardian Tools were deposited into the tower storage. Adding to the rewards he got from the tower, he summoned ten powerful metallic beings, each radiating no aura, but just staring at them showed they were dangerous.
"This will do for now. As for the materials to upgrade them, I will give the list to the king; this is a High World—they will have more than a Medium World could offer."
Kent nodded with satisfaction.

So far, as a guardian, he had already ensured the future of those he was protecting was catered for. The only thing left was for him to get back to his business and watch his Soul Essence rise every damn second.
"This is the best," Kent smiled and vanished back to Fedora.

chapters.title: Chapter 628: Before Entering Seclusion (1) [Bonus]
paragraphs: "So you ladies want to spend a week here, huh?" Kent asked, sitting with his women in Dori’s house. They had just told him they would spend a week there before returning to the tower.
Of course, using outside time, a week was not that long, but compared to tower time, a week was equivalent to many months inside the tower.
That was a lot of time wasted. However, it wasn’t as if they were wasting it for nothing.
They were waiting for Princess Lovina to complete her tempering, then they would enter the Primordial Chamber and initiate the awakening of the Primordial Spirit.
It would take close to 30 years for that to end, but he had a feeling they would come out powerful. Spending a week outside before entering was already enough for him to understand their request.
In the end, he let them stay.
After spending hours with them, he went to see the king one last time.

"These are all Spirit King-grade battle dolls. I will set them at the borders, so you can pull back some of your guards and assign the trustworthy ones to patrol with these dolls," Kent said, introducing the Guardian Swordsmen and Archers to the king, who was very shocked but happy to have such amazing battle dolls.

Kent took out a scroll and handed it to the king. "This is how to upgrade them and the materials required. If you manage to get even five out of the ten items, you can upgrade them to Tier 15, which is the Spirit Emperor stage.
However, even without such extreme upgrades, they are still amazing, so don’t hesitate to use them whenever there is trouble while I am away."
"Thank you, Kent. You really saved me and my people," King Hkum said with a grateful expression. Kent nodded and stood up.

"Oh, before I forget, you can give some of the Ambrosia apples to your allies. I don’t know how much you trust them, but if that trust is enough, then go ahead and give them some." With that, Kent vanished.
The king and his elders exchanged a glance and a sigh.

"Yet again, our supreme advisor has made sure we got the better end of the deal. This is just too great. With this, not only will we soon have the power to counter the Orc alliance, but we can start moving around the world again and even travel outside," King Hkum said.
The elders nodded.
"This is all thanks to Kent. He has indeed brought a change to us," Elder Jorin said. The other elders smiled, hearing words they would forever speak about to the generations yet to come.
"The queen and the children have already entered seclusion; you five should do the same. I have already broken a limit, so I don’t need to enter seclusion urgently.
I will help Ashfur handle the array before doing so. By then, the queen will be out, and she can hold down the fort while I also enter seclusion."
The elders couldn’t argue that. They should truly enter seclusion because when the time comes, they will be the ones facing the most danger.

"Also, about our allies, I have already decided to give them two each for now. Although we are allies, I still have my reservations, so for now, I will provide them with two each. When we see progress in the alliance, we can add more.
Also, General Ragnar has selected 25 trusted soldiers, each a Spirit King, to receive the fruit, so I think we will have more in reserve for now."
The elders nodded and then fine-tuned some details before retiring to seclusion. When the king was left alone, he sighed and then leaned back in his throne.
"Kent Madson, just what kind of existence are you?" His question remained unanswered as he vanished the next second and appeared inside a room where his wife was cultivating the Ambrosia apple.
He sealed the room, then went ahead and did the same for his children before leaving. As he said, with the elders and his wife in seclusion, he would ensure that no harm came to anyone.
Kent also went back to his wives and chose to spend another day with them.
At this point, the Foxkin already knew there were humans in their land, so when Kent and his wives went to a restaurant to eat, they didn’t face any injustice.
Kent spent the day shopping with his wives, eating, and visiting the best places in Emberwood. They even went outside into the Yellow Maple Forest and had some fun there before returning to the city.
After spending the night with them, he returned to the tower. Sword King Shawn had already entered seclusion and was busy at work, so Kent didn’t bother with him before he left.
He already knew he would be gone for months, perhaps a year, so he just left.

Kent quickly appeared in the Tower City to inform Elaine’s parents, who are considered leaders of the humans in the tower, and Tribe Chief Malthar of the Bloodvein tribe that he would be gone for some years.
Since time ran differently inside the tower, they knew the years he was referring to would be equivalent to months on the outside.
"Don’t worry, Kent, we already have everything we need," Lady Rain said after Kent informed them of his plan for the next couple of years.
"Alright. However, if you need anything, Gaia and her sisters are there to assist you. Just let them know." They nodded, and Kent walked away.
After he left, he went straight to the Legion Tower.
"Master, are we going on another mission?" As expected, Kaizo was the first to notice his presence and immediately asked what he wanted to know.
Kent just smiled, regretting that he had made the brute unyielding and always hungry for battle. "You should get yourself a woman, Kaizo. Why is it always about battle to you?"
The undead and the Dungeon bosses laughed. Kaizo was the same, too. Kent looked at them and shook his head.
"I will be entering seclusion soon, but before that, why don’t I upgrade you all?"

chapters.title: Chapter 629: Before Entering Seclusion (2) [Bonus]
paragraphs: The battle that happened at the Hound Barracks and the Lionkin stronghold has generated a rather sizable income in the form of Tower points.
Currently, Kent is swimming in Tower points.
So, his first order of business was to upgrade his 12 Dungeon Bosses. Each one of the dungeons requires 100 million Tower points to upgrade from SS to SSS.
This means that the moment the dungeons are upgraded, more levels will be added, and the strength of the last floor bosses will also increase.
They will be at the peak of the Core Formation stage, something he needed for his mission to save Planet Dusk. He wanted them ready for battle any day.
"The plan at first was for me to come out of seclusion before upgrading you all, but knowing I will be gone for a while, I will do that now.

This means the dungeons will be upgraded, and as such, you all will also get a boost in your strength. So, your first task after the upgrades is to use the dungeons to train, sharpen your skills, and wait for me to emerge from seclusion.
The moment I finish my tasks, I will take you to a new place where we will encounter some of the strongest beings you can face in a medium world.
Of course, we have already faced armies from a high world, so you all would think armies from a medium world are beneath you.
But I beg to differ. The dungeon we will face is one of the most dangerous places you can enter in a medium world, so be prepared."
They all nodded.
Kent wasn’t exaggerating.
The quest to save Planet Dusk is something he knew would be harrowing, so he aspires to raise the strength of his legion first. He had a feeling the danger waiting for them was not going to be easy.
"The moment I start the upgrade, you all will go to sleep for a while, so you can enter your dungeons now." The Dungeon Bosses nodded.
Kent already knew of Valtor’s condition and knew that after the upgrade, he would wake up, stronger than ever. Once the Dungeon Bosses left, Kent turned to the Undead.
"Akira will see to your upgrades. Yours too will take some time, so when you are done, use the dungeons to train. And Zareth, you can use the chance to unlock more of your inheritance.

I saw what you can do even against Spirit Ascension stage experts. I have a feeling that the mission we will embark on after I am out of seclusion will require you to be at your strongest, so you should all prepare well.
Gaia will add eight more friends while I am away, so make them feel comfortable." The Undead Legions nodded.
Kent turned to the cocoon housing the Hunter, who was now undergoing her evolution to become a Dragon Necromancer, someone who can summon only undead dragons.
Kent had a feeling she would wake up with a surprise, so he asked his Undead Legion to pay attention to her when she is out and make her feel welcome while he is away.
After he was done with them, he went to see his three assistants.
⟪We will miss you, master.⟫ Gaia said, clinging to Kent’s leg, not wanting him to leave. Akira was doing the same to his other leg, while Dori held his clothes.
"Relax, you three, it is not like I am going away for good. I will be inside the Sword Tower, the Soul Tower, or the Alchemy Tower. You can come and watch me if you want," Kent said with a laugh.
⟪That is not the same. We would miss playing wrestling with you,⟫ Dori said. He knew they enjoyed wrestling with him, but hearing them say it made him sigh inwardly.
"Then how about this? When I am out of seclusion, we can wrestle for an entire week and even go ice skating too... if you can build one."
⟪Really?⟫ They all asked.
"Yes. I’ll play with you all for as long as you’d like. So, what do you say?" Kent asked, and the three lolis smiled cheerfully.
⟪It is a deal, master. We will wait for you to emerge from seclusion. And don’t worry, we will handle the undead creations while you are away.⟫
Kent nodded at their words.
They had eight more undead to create using the undead schematic. As for resources, he had more than enough to make them very powerful, so Kent didn’t doubt they would indeed get the job done well.

"If you are bored, you can go to Fedora and play with the little fox princess. I am sure she will be happy to meet Lady Tala’s friends," Kent said with a laugh before vanishing from the mountain garden.
He knew her sisters would torment her to tell them all about Lady Tala, so he left before she could set her murderous sight on him.
The first thing Kent did when he entered the Sword Tower was to sacrifice 1.2 billion Tower points to upgrade the dungeons.
⟦Congratulations on upgrading your dungeons from SS ↠ SSS⟧
⟦Upgrade will take 120 days⟧
⟦The floors of the dungeons will increase from 10 ↠ 17⟧
"Looks like this will keep them busy for the next couple of months while I am away." Kent nodded with satisfaction and then checked his remaining balance.
[Attribute Points: 1,090,900]
[Tower Points: 970,400,000]
[Skill Upgrade Points: 911,100]
⟦Soul Essence: 1,270,900,600⟧
A smile appeared on his lips. "It has already been a couple of hours, but it seems the Foxkins are much harder working than I thought."
Watching the Soul Essence grow was enough to make him happy. It turned out that he hadn’t wasted his wealth for nothing.
After ensuring everything was in order, he turned his attention to his tasks.
"First, I will review Jest’s memories, all three of them, and then move on to the Chaos Dragons’ memories, and then the Faceless Assassin.
Afterward, I will handle the Soul Path before ending with Alchemy. By then, my wives will be out of seclusion, and the legion will become stronger.
They can even start handling the dungeon in Dusk while I find my way into the Supreme Immortal Sect and challenge the Pill Princess.
I only hope she lives up to the hype, for I won’t be coming out a wannabe Alchemist. It is time for the Perfect Alchemist to rise and dominate the entire universe."
Kent sighed and retrieved the first memory key...

Kent turned to the cocoon housing the Hunter, who was now undergoing her evolution to become a Dragon Necromancer, someone who can summon only undead dragons.
Kent had a feeling she would wake up with a surprise, so he asked his Undead Legion to pay attention to her when she is out and make her feel welcome while he is away.
After he was done with them, he went to see his three assistants.
⟪We will miss you, master.⟫ Gaia said, clinging to Kent’s leg, not wanting him to leave.
Akira was doing the same to his other leg, while Dori held his clothes.
"Relax, you three, it is not like I am going away for good.
I will be inside the Sword Tower, the Soul Tower, or the Alchemy Tower.
You can come and watch me if you want," Kent said with a laugh.
⟪That is not the same.
We would miss playing wrestling with you,⟫ Dori said.
He knew they enjoyed wrestling with him, but hearing them say it made him sigh inwardly.
"Then how about this?
When I am out of seclusion, we can wrestle for an entire week and even go ice skating too... if you can build one."
⟪Really?⟫ They all asked.
"Yes.
I’ll play with you all for as long as you’d like.
So, what do you say?" Kent asked, and the three lolis smiled cheerfully.
⟪It is a deal, master.
We will wait for you to emerge from seclusion.
And don’t worry, we will handle the undead creations while you are away.⟫
Kent nodded at their words.
They had eight more undead to create using the undead schematic.
As for resources, he had more than enough to make them very powerful, so Kent didn’t doubt they would indeed get the job done well.
"If you are bored, you can go to Fedora and play with the little fox princess.
I am sure she will be happy to meet Lady Tala’s friends," Kent said with a laugh before vanishing from the mountain garden.
He knew her sisters would torment her to tell them all about Lady Tala, so he left before she could set her murderous sight on him.
The first thing Kent did when he entered the Sword Tower was to sacrifice 1.2 billion Tower points to upgrade the dungeons.
⟦Congratulations on upgrading your dungeons from SS ↠ SSS⟧
⟦Upgrade will take 120 days⟧
⟦The floors of the dungeons will increase from 10 ↠ 17⟧
"Looks like this will keep them busy for the next couple of months while I am away." Kent nodded with satisfaction and then checked his remaining balance.
[Attribute Points: 1,090,900]
[Tower Points: 970,400,000]
[Skill Upgrade Points: 911,100]
⟦Soul Essence: 1,270,900,600⟧
A smile appeared on his lips.
"It has already been a couple of hours, but it seems the Foxkins are much harder working than I thought."
Watching the Soul Essence grow was enough to make him happy.
It turned out that he hadn’t wasted his wealth for nothing.
After ensuring everything was in order, he turned his attention to his tasks.
"First, I will review Jest’s memories, all three of them, and then move on to the Chaos Dragons’ memories, and then the Faceless Assassin.
Afterward, I will handle the Soul Path before ending with Alchemy.
By then, my wives will be out of seclusion, and the legion will become stronger.
They can even start handling the dungeon in Dusk while I find my way into the Supreme Immortal Sect and challenge the Pill Princess.
I only hope she lives up to the hype, for I won’t be coming out a wannabe Alchemist.
It is time for the Perfect Alchemist to rise and dominate the entire universe."
Kent sighed and retrieved the first memory key...

chapters.title: Chapter 630: The Path Forward [Bonus]
paragraphs: Jest emerged from the Dao Realm a different person.

He spent 20 years in an enlightened state, still inside the Sword Valley. When he woke up, he felt like he had what it took to surpass all else. He felt that his time to rise had come, so he left and began to walk his path.
However, 20 more years passed, and he hadn’t even moved a single step on his sword path. Aside from becoming the best Sword Saint there is, he hadn’t made any progress.
"I clearly know what has to be done, but why am I not making any progress even after 20 years?" Jest wondered. He didn’t know why.
The plan was to reach the peak, yet even after such a breakthrough, he made no progress. It was a blow to his ego as a swordsman.
But Jest was a patient man. He had been patient for years, so he could be patient again. Thus, another ten years passed, but still there was no progress.
At this point, his patience was wearing thin, so when he heard someone had become a sword emperor, it was a blow to him.

"Why... I ventured into the realm of the Dao, saw the Dao face-to-face, and even gained enlightenment, so why can’t I make progress on my path? Am I destined to fail?" Jest was in a state of breakdown at this point.
What he didn’t know, however, was that meeting the Dao and returning alive was a blessing to the entire Universe and a curse to him.
Some things are not meant to happen.
One of them is talking to Laws (Dao). But Jest did, and that was his curse, yet a blessing to everyone else. So, while he was struggling, his peers and the new generation were making progress.
By the time Jest turned 100 years old, he was ready to give up.
However, he still had a promise he couldn’t bring himself to break.
"I can’t go on like this," he said. He knew if he gave up, the slave mine would forever be there, and he wouldn’t be able to do anything to save his family.
He knew that, though they might think he was dead, he wouldn’t be able to forgive himself if he just gave up.
His dream of saving them would also wash away with his failure.
So he went into seclusion, and this time, he made a promise to himself—one that would stick with him for the years to come.
"I will be the first to reach the peak."
The legend of Lord Genesis wasn’t one that saw him rise to the peak alone; it was one that saw him be the first to reach the peak.

There were others, but only he reached the peak, and this was due to a decision that one day would be called the Primordial Path, as opposed to the one he had tried to walk and failed—the Primitive Path.
Before, he was walking the Primitive Path, one that was good but not the best. This time, he aspired to walk his own path, and to do that, he had to fight against his destiny.
In other words, he had to fight against the Dao, and that began when he made up his mind. He decided to walk the path he deemed fit for him.
Thus, the sword mind was formed. His five years in seclusion were all about creating the various ways a swordsman can parry.
It was said that the day he came out, a single parry of his sword could cleave through any defense and shatter any sword.

A determined man, focused keenly on perfecting just parrying with his sword, and the result was wild. So he entered seclusion again, and for ten more years, he took the parry to a new level, ultimately turning it into something known as the Single Swing.
When he stood before the Slave Mine, a single swing was all it took to bring the whole place down. He fulfilled his promise and saved his people.
But that was when his life took a chaotic turn. The first ten years after he destroyed the slave mine, he was chased down by a powerful cultivator.
He killed most, and from many he ran. However, he never lost a fight.
He had indeed made many enemies, but never in his wildest dreams did he think that with a single determined mindset, he would be able to create a decisive sword move.
So, on the run, Jest created the first 15 sword moves, which evolved into 50 over the next few months, and then 1,000 the following year.
By the end of the tenth year, he had made 1,600,000 sword moves, laying the foundation for the Genesis sword path.
The foundation of the Genesis sword path was one of the most robust and perhaps the most sturdy in the history of the universe.

Jest then went ahead and built upon his foundation, taking his sword path from the novice stage to the Sword King stage, finally awakening the Heavenly Sword aura and intent. It was at this point that the legend of the Mind Swordsman started to rise.
They said he practiced his sword in his mind, and regardless of how good you were, a single glance was all he needed to master your sword moves.

This wasn’t because Jest was a machine. No, it was because, in his quest to create the foundation for his sword path, he had mastered every possible sword move there could be. Every calculation, every possibility—everything was included in his 1.6 million sword moves.

So he became someone who could master any swordplay with just a glance. His legend reached its peak, and while nobody said it, his importance on the path of the sword—or as most said, the path of the weapon—was supreme.
By the time Jest turned 200 years old, he had become a Sword Emperor, someone who stood at the pinnacle of his world. He was respected and loved by all.
But Jest knew there were more paths to rise to and more adventures to be had. So he decided to travel to the immortal worlds, where the dangers were much more harrowing.

chapters.title: Chapter 631: Way to The Immortal Worlds [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent emerged from the memory to a message that made him smile.
⟦Congratulations on mastering all 1,600,000 sword moves of the Genesis Path⟧
"So that is what all this was about. I knew reviewing this memory would be very helpful." Kent’s smile widened as he felt his body grow sharper, almost like he had become a weapon itself.

"I bet Jest never expected that one day he would need his own hard work to rise swiftly through the starry skies." If Jest were present, he would probably smack Kent silly for riding nonchalantly on his hard work.
But that is what he signed up for when he reincarnated, so he can blame himself for bringing it on.
"But to think I wasn’t the sole swordsman to rise through the ranks, it seems I underestimated the brilliance of many.

Just that they all couldn’t get to the peak, simply because the path they walked was limited, unlike mine. In other words, I should be called the father of the Primordial Sword Path, not the father of swordsmen.

But then again, I understand. I did not only pick the path that led to the peak, I also showed everyone there are different ways out there, and that following someone’s path won’t necessarily make you the greatest."
Kent sighed.
"But how the fuck is Jest going to get to an immortal world when he searched years but couldn’t find a path?" This question made Kent take out the second key and press it against his forehead.
However, instead of entering yet another memory, a diary appeared in his hand.
The title on it read, "Jest Diary 1/9."

"I see. So all the immersive memories were so that I could inherit the 1.6 memories," Kent concluded. However, there was something about the diary that made him feel like it was more than just a book.
Nevertheless, Kent flipped it open and started to read.
[So I found a way to get into the immortal worlds. However, I need to travel back to the Sword Valley and enter the no man’s land.
Of course, this sounds like a bad idea, but the only way to get to the immortal world is to break the last sword move left by the genius swordsmen of the primordial era.
I might die; however, knowing my people are safe and those responsible for slave trading are dealt with, I feel like dying is not too bad.
I know I’m a lunatic, but I have a feeling my reincarnations will be even more eccentric than I. So what can I say? It is genetics, I guess..."_"]
"This bastard," Kent smiled, feeling amused by something he had written himself—well, a more lunatic version of himself who lived billions of years ago.
"But I guess he has a point. The slaves were the priority; whatever crazy thing we did after that is just us being stupid.
Though I dare ask, doesn’t he have a girlfriend? Then again, I saw his life, and even after 250 years, he is still single and a virgin. Can’t wait to hear when he will get laid."
Kent burst out laughing like a maniac. It wasn’t every day a person gets amused by their past self’s sex life. But then again, it is Kent, the Shameless Dragon.
He turned back to the diary.

[At long last, I arrived at the Crossing. However, the no man’s land is no easy place to traverse. I am a Sword Emperor and a Spirit King, but the beasts here are just too much for even a Spirit Emperor to handle.

The last beast I killed was a Spirit Lord who had mastered the Flame to the Perfect stage. I nearly died, and while I managed to kill it in the end, to my future self, if you are reading this, never fight a Mountain Flame Goat if you don’t have control over any flame art.
But I survived, and this time, I am a step away from seeing immortals. Although I must say, I wonder what they look like, what they wear, and how they talk.
I’m not particularly skilled in fashion, of course. Aunty Emri made sure I took the best clothes she had at her store, but what if I look like a beggar in the immortal worlds?
Aaah, this is a headache... However, I will probably have to adapt more quickly before I become a laughingstock to some young immortals.
Lord knows I would love to shut them up with my sword.
Ultimately, violence is the means. Okay, bye for now, I want to see if my life is a hardy or a softy.]

"True Jest, your dressing sucks. No wonder no lady showed any interest in you. Though Aunty Emri indeed made you look more like a bachelor, I wonder how you will adapt in an immortal world," Kent laughed.
"That goat really handed your ass to—"
"Wait, how am I remembering something I am reading as if I were there and saw everything?" Kent immediately recognized something was happening.
It was as if, as he was reading, he appeared to be there, witnessing everything, just as he had when he was immersed in Jest memories. It felt as though he was reliving the memories.
"Dori, what is happening?" Kent had to call a lawyer.
⟪Why doesn’t the master finish reading the diary first? The answer will come when you finish everything. Me telling you will just spoil the fun⟫
Kent sighed and then returned to the diary.
[Well, that is just great. So it turns out that to break the sword move and create the spatial channel, I must first master the sword techniques used in the attack.
I studied it, and when I gained access to the essence of the sword technique, the owner of the sword’s move appeared in the form of divine consciousness.
He said his name was Immortal Monarch Liu Yang, the sect leader of the Transcendent Sword sect, and the sword move he used is the second form of the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique.

He gave me the whole technique, and I must master the first two stages. So, I guess it’s back to the No Man’s Land, then. I need to fight stronger monsters now, and I doubt I will come out alive this time.
...Wish me luck.]

chapters.title: Chapter 632: Entering an Immortal World [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Finally... After five years of audacious death battles, I finally managed to combine ten swords, forming a single powerful sword that can literally cleave through the void and create spatial channels.

I must say, the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique is remarkably powerful. I struggle even to begin to fathom how unfathomable it is. I spent every single day thinking about how someone could create something this powerful.
It has seven forms, and even the first two forms helped me defeat beings far stronger than me.
...Oh, I fought another Mountain Flame Goat, a peak Spirit King, but ended it in a single blow using just the first form of the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique.
Now that I think about it, the single blow was more like ten three-meter-long swords that were formed using Sword Qi and imbued with the power of sword intent.
Even my heavenly sword aura and intent weren’t up to standard, but it was already enough to accomplish my goal, so this is where I hang the towel and be on my way.
...By the way, ignore what I said years back... If you meet a Mountain Flame Goat, be sure to have your spices ready. Their meat is tender and smells great... hehe.]
Kent chuckled, then closed the diary and stood up. He walked forward and stopped. The next second, he conjured a golden sword, making it appear in the air above him.
Then a second sword appeared, followed by the third. Soon, seven swords hovered above him, but a pale look appeared on his face. A few seconds later, the swords vanished, and Kent took a deep sigh.

"I need to learn Heavenly Sword Energy first; only then can I use all ten swords. But even now, just one sword is already enough to make a difference, and I can conjure seven." A smile appeared on his face.
He walked back and sat down in front of the Sword of Enlightenment. The diary appeared in his hand, and then he continued to read.
The Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique is rather complex. It requires a great understanding of sword energy.
That was why it took Jest five years to master the first two forms of the technique despite being a Sword Emperor.
But who can blame him? To master the sword technique, Jest needed to advance his understanding of sword energy to some extent.
This would allow him to form ten 3-meter swords. For the second form, he must put all ten swords together to create a 4-meter sword. Then, for the third form, he must form a 4-meter sword.
This means the first form must be mastered to 100 swords, which will give him ten swords at the second form, which will form the one 4-meter-long sword at the third stage.

This alone demonstrates the complexity and incredible power of the technique. But if mastered to the seventh form, then perhaps Kent would learn the full power of the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique.
[Ah, it feels good to be back here. Now, all I need to do is use the second move, and I will be on my way to the immortal worlds.
But before I leave, I must first say something... God only knows today will be the last time I will be able to express myself freely.
First, I don’t know why Divine came before Immortal in the sword path, but I intend to find out.

Second, I just want to say that if I ever don’t return to Byrmrr, I would want the heavens to know that this is my origin. So, if I somehow become a legend in the future, remember to preserve my heritage.
You wouldn’t want me coming back to hunt you... hehe, just kidding. But I am serious, so hold Byrmrr dear and we won’t have any issues.
On that note... Immortals, here I come.]
Kent closed the book. However, the moment he did, it disassembled into sparks of light and flew into his mind. The next instant, a powerful, profound sword energy burst forth from his body.
Kent’s consciousness was pulled into the realm of enlightenment. He had just entered his third sword enlightenment.

The first happened after reviewing Jest’s second memory packet, and now, the fourth memory had sent him into an enlightened state. Even as the minutes started to pass, his sword energy seemed to grow.

He is required to have achieved seven enlightenments out of eleven before he can become a Sword Saint. So far, he is on his third, and from what happened, it seems to have something to do with the diary he had read.
A year went by, and Kent remained in his enlightened state. Slowly, the years started passing. Seven years into the Enlightenment, a powerful aura burst out of his body, raising him into the air.
Up in the air, ten golden swords, each three meters long, appeared. Then, slowly, they merged into one four-meter-long sword. It hovered in the air for a few minutes before dispersing.
Kent then opened his eyes, and a smile appeared on his lips. "Looks like all I needed was insight from the real owner of the technique."
During the Enlightenment, he appeared in the Sword Valley, where he met the true Immortal Monarch, Liu Yang, the creator of the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique.
He gave him some insight, and then he was required to break the sword move that Jest broke before he could leave the enlightenment.
It took him seven years, but he succeeded as a Sword Grandmaster, while Jest took five years to become a Sword Emperor.
Kent laughed, but he understood that he had only gotten this far thanks to Jest’s determination.

"Looks like the diary is the key to gaining enlightenment. In that case, why not dive into the last memory? This will then leave me with seven more memories of Jest to go through." He was ecstatic to know more, so he took out the last key.
That one, too, turned into a diary. The same title was inscribed on it: "Jest Diary 2/9."
"Here we go again." Reading the diary made Kent very happy, so he couldn’t wait to read more.

sentences.text: [Finally...
After five years of audacious death battles, I finally managed to combine ten swords, forming a single powerful sword that can literally cleave through the void and create spatial channels.
I must say, the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique is remarkably powerful.
I struggle even to begin to fathom how unfathomable it is.
I spent every single day thinking about how someone could create something this powerful.
It has seven forms, and even the first two forms helped me defeat beings far stronger than me.
...Oh, I fought another Mountain Flame Goat, a peak Spirit King, but ended it in a single blow using just the first form of the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique.
Now that I think about it, the single blow was more like ten three-meter-long swords that were formed using Sword Qi and imbued with the power of sword intent.
Even my heavenly sword aura and intent weren’t up to standard, but it was already enough to accomplish my goal, so this is where I hang the towel and be on my way.
...By the way, ignore what I said years back...
If you meet a Mountain Flame Goat, be sure to have your spices ready.
Their meat is tender and smells great... hehe.]
Kent chuckled, then closed the diary and stood up.
He walked forward and stopped.
The next second, he conjured a golden sword, making it appear in the air above him.
Then a second sword appeared, followed by the third.
Soon, seven swords hovered above him, but a pale look appeared on his face.
A few seconds later, the swords vanished, and Kent took a deep sigh.
"I need to learn Heavenly Sword Energy first; only then can I use all ten swords.
But even now, just one sword is already enough to make a difference, and I can conjure seven." A smile appeared on his face.
He walked back and sat down in front of the Sword of Enlightenment.
The diary appeared in his hand, and then he continued to read.
The Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique is rather complex.
It requires a great understanding of sword energy.
That was why it took Jest five years to master the first two forms of the technique despite being a Sword Emperor.
But who can blame him?
To master the sword technique, Jest needed to advance his understanding of sword energy to some extent.
This would allow him to form ten 3-meter swords.
For the second form, he must put all ten swords together to create a 4-meter sword.
Then, for the third form, he must form a 4-meter sword.
This means the first form must be mastered to 100 swords, which will give him ten swords at the second form, which will form the one 4-meter-long sword at the third stage.
This alone demonstrates the complexity and incredible power of the technique.
But if mastered to the seventh form, then perhaps Kent would learn the full power of the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique.
[Ah, it feels good to be back here.
Now, all I need to do is use the second move, and I will be on my way to the immortal worlds.
But before I leave, I must first say something...
God only knows today will be the last time I will be able to express myself freely.
First, I don’t know why Divine came before Immortal in the sword path, but I intend to find out.
Second, I just want to say that if I ever don’t return to Byrmrr, I would want the heavens to know that this is my origin.
So, if I somehow become a legend in the future, remember to preserve my heritage.
You wouldn’t want me coming back to hunt you... hehe, just kidding.
But I am serious, so hold Byrmrr dear and we won’t have any issues.
On that note...
Immortals, here I come.]
Kent closed the book.
However, the moment he did, it disassembled into sparks of light and flew into his mind.
The next instant, a powerful, profound sword energy burst forth from his body.
Kent’s consciousness was pulled into the realm of enlightenment.
He had just entered his third sword enlightenment.
The first happened after reviewing Jest’s second memory packet, and now, the fourth memory had sent him into an enlightened state.
Even as the minutes started to pass, his sword energy seemed to grow.
He is required to have achieved seven enlightenments out of eleven before he can become a Sword Saint.
So far, he is on his third, and from what happened, it seems to have something to do with the diary he had read.
A year went by, and Kent remained in his enlightened state.
Slowly, the years started passing.
Seven years into the Enlightenment, a powerful aura burst out of his body, raising him into the air.
Up in the air, ten golden swords, each three meters long, appeared.
Then, slowly, they merged into one four-meter-long sword.
It hovered in the air for a few minutes before dispersing.
Kent then opened his eyes, and a smile appeared on his lips.
"Looks like all I needed was insight from the real owner of the technique."
During the Enlightenment, he appeared in the Sword Valley, where he met the true Immortal Monarch, Liu Yang, the creator of the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique.
He gave him some insight, and then he was required to break the sword move that Jest broke before he could leave the enlightenment.
It took him seven years, but he succeeded as a Sword Grandmaster, while Jest took five years to become a Sword Emperor.
Kent laughed, but he understood that he had only gotten this far thanks to Jest’s determination.
"Looks like the diary is the key to gaining enlightenment.
In that case, why not dive into the last memory?
This will then leave me with seven more memories of Jest to go through." He was ecstatic to know more, so he took out the last key.
That one, too, turned into a diary.
The same title was inscribed on it: "Jest Diary 2/9."
"Here we go again." Reading the diary made Kent very happy, so he couldn’t wait to read more.

chapters.title: Chapter 633: Impossible Situation [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Guess what? I made it to an immortal world... but there is a big problem... I’m in an impossible situation here. How should I go about this...
Well, it goes like this. After I destroyed the sword move left by Immortal Monarch, Yiu Yang, and entered the spatial channel, I found myself in an immortal world.
I knew it was an immortal world because the air was different.
It was richer and more potent. So I knew it was an immortal world right away. I later learned its name was Eryndor — a vast world housing diverse races.
The reason I said I found myself in an impossible situation was because I woke up in a prison cell after the travel that took years or maybe a few seconds.
I truly can’t tell you how long it took, because I passed out the moment I entered the spatial channel.
The place I woke up in was the Yushen Plateau — The Realm of the Celestial Beasts. It is one of the five continents in Eryndor.
Yushen Plateau is the realm of the beastkins. I found myself in the Moonfang Tiger Clan, one of the four main Beast Clans there.
One would wonder why I was imprisoned. It turns out the Beasts are in a hundred-year-old war with the humans, and as such, I was a war prisoner.
The irony in that.

But I was trapped, and since I can’t escape considering the guards are even Spirit Lords, I knew I was fucked. For ten years, I remained in prison, cultivating and advancing my cultivation base to the peak of the Spirit King stage.
I knew that if my cultivation base reached the Spirit Emperor or Spirit Sovereign stage, I might be able to escape, but it turned out they had an immortal there who was keeping a close eye on me.
One strange part is that she hates swordsmen, so you can see where I found myself.

My dream of exploring the immortal worlds has now left me shackled simply because of my bad luck: I appeared in a place at war with my kind, and even worse, the immortal I couldn’t contend against also hated my profession.
Talk about bad luck...]
Kent couldn’t help laughing as he flipped to the second page of the diary. Though Jest was probably scared for his life back then, Kent couldn’t help laughing.
"I guess his bad luck was rather strong."
[So it has already been 50 years since I was captured and imprisoned on Yushen Plateau. That means I spent 50 years of my life in the immortal world as a prisoner.
But guess what? I am a free man.
I know, right? The immortal lady who never ever allowed me a drop of water for the past 50 years died, and her death was rather pitiful.
It turns out that humans are even more evil than the Abysskin hidden in the Netherveil Abyss. And yes, that is another continent in Eryndor.
Naturally, the humans were stronger than the Beastkins; however, because the beasts knew their territory well, it took the humans 150 years to finally break the blockade.
When they arrived at the city of the Tigerkin, only the immortal lady remained. She faced three human immortals, and after three hours of battle, she was ripped limb from limb.

Thankfully, after the battle was over, I was rescued by an immortal whose name I will never forget — a true immortal, called Yusif. Being human myself, I was taken to Verdantia, the Land of the Elemental Humans.
It was a nice continent. It had five cities named Elemental Cities. It turns out that in this immortal world, there are five types of humans.
Ice, Fire, Water, Earth, and Lightning. Everyone born has the chance to awaken one of the five elements. True Immortal Yusif was from the Fire City, so he took me there.
He gave me a few spirit stones, a much higher version of the ones I had, and set me off.
He told me that if I wanted to practice swordsmanship, I should go to a different immortal world because in Eryndor, only the Elves know swordsmanship, and they don’t like humans.
I took his words to heart, and so I decided to prepare before going. Since the humans are welcoming, I stayed in Fire City for three years, which helped me become a Spirit Emperor.
Thankfully, I managed to reach the third stage of the Transcendent Heavenly Sword Technique.
This gave me the confidence to purchase my seat on the spatial boat that travels to the World of Valyrion: The Realm of the Eternal Blade. The ship travels every five years.
I wouldn’t have to take the spatial channel with my physical body again. It turns out that doing so without a good grasp of space law is very dangerous. I was lucky I survived the first time.
With two years to go, I spent a few months exploring Eryndor before retiring to wait for the ship to arrive.
Immortal worlds are weird. It turns out there is a world for anything. There are thousands of worlds where only the sword is practiced.
Valyrion is such a world. It has four continents, each in competition with the other.
I didn’t know which one to visit, but I planned on joining the one that matches my sword path — well, my sword path complements everything, considering it was my creation.
But I planned to have a quiet life there and raise my sword path to the never-ending level. That was a well-planned life, yet again. This time, I knew I wouldn’t end up in prison.
It turns out that my life was about to get even worse than what had happened to me when I first arrived in Eryndor.
When I said bye-byes to True Immortal Yusif, I entered the ship that took three years to get to Valyrion.

I arrived in Shengdao City, the capital of the Bladeheart continent. I didn’t know what awaited me there, but it turns out that if you step into that godforsaken city, if you don’t want to be challenged, then put away your sword.
I didn’t know that, and that was how I came to know Seraphina, the Moonlit Dancer — the woman who would chase me all over Valyrion and beyond.
I will spend thousands of years running from her, for she aims to kill me. The reason was that I refused to accept her challenge... a grave crime.]
Kent closed the book, and his consciousness was drawn back into the realm of enlightenment once again...His fourth enlightenment was underway.

chapters.title: Chapter 634: Progress after five Memories [Bonus]
paragraphs: After reading the second diary, Kent entered yet another enlightenment. This meant his understanding of the sword had deepened yet again, and that was something that made him very happy.
This time, he lasted only five years in the enlightenment, but when he came out, his profound sword energy had reached Level 2. Thus, his sword intent and aura had reached the Level 2 profound stage.
"Who would have thought a mere diary could make me gain two enlightenments just like that? This, of course, means I must get the rest of my memories back..."
A rare smile appeared on his lips as he gazed at the large sword bridge and wondered just how many levels he could traverse this time.

He had already cleared the first four levels, so he wanted to know how much further he could move this time. While he had indeed become stronger, the sword bridge adapted to his strength, so there was no telling how many levels he could go next time he faced it.
"I have already fulfilled two of the requirements to become a sword saint." Kent sighed, stood up, and started walking about.
"I have already comprehended all 10,002 sword moves — well, I have comprehended all 1.6 million sword moves thanks to Jest, so this means I won’t be getting tasks on that anymore.
Aside from that, I have also unlocked profound sword energy, another requirement in the long list required of me." Kent shook his head and took out an ambrosia apple and bit into it.
He savored the taste, feeling the energy wash through his body. After walking around for a few minutes, he sat back down.
"I am left with three more enlightenments to fulfill these requirements, too. However, attaining all eleven enlightenments before becoming a sword saint would be something not even Jest had attained.

I am required to get only seven. Jest attained five, something that made him a monster on the sword path. If I can gain all eleven instead of just the seven required of me, I will become even more monstrous."
He lay back and stared at the blue sky and the 13 moons above.
"I should really force myself to gain all 11; this way, I will become someone who has set his own records." Kent meant his words, and as such, he was determined to get it done.
He truly wanted to see how far he could take the sword path, considering he was someone who had once reached the peak.
However, when he reached the peak, the question he asked himself then was whether the peak he reached was truly the peak.
The peak is the Celestial Sword stage, where the sword intent, aura, sword gaze, sword body, sword realm, and other aspects of swordsmanship converge to form a stage called the Sword Will.
This stage transcends one’s understanding to a level known as One with the Sword—the will of the sword. He had reached that stage once, but he was determined to know where he could go from there.
"The next most important requirement is to traverse the sword bridge and form the three sword technique foundations.
I know Jest was obsessed with creating his sword technique; however, he never truly figured it out, even after spending 50 years in prison. He had the time, but he couldn’t even create one.
However, I think I can do it. It will take some time, but I have an idea now that I need to ponder," Kent sighed and lifted his body to sit down in the lotus posture.
One good thing about the sword mind part of his sword path was that he could visualize anything in his mind, in a real sort of way.
This realm allowed him to visualize what he wanted to achieve, and if he was satisfied, it would assimilate into his body.
Kent didn’t really know if his idea would work, so he just started to visualize the foundation of his first sword technique.
However, even after four months, he came out empty-handed. It was like whenever he was getting close to a breakthrough, a part of him rejected the idea.
Perhaps he was thinking too shallowly, but the feeling of failure didn’t taste too good either. However, consistent failure made him understand one thing:
"I am still lacking. I need to witness more sword battles and participate in loads of them," Kent smirked.
"I doubt the Everlasting Immortal Sword Sect Val will be of any use. However, I have a feeling I will gain some insight when I get to the other continents.

Perhaps the Supreme Immortal Sect will have something to offer." Kent didn’t have much hope in them either. He needed to be in a challenging environment. However, sometimes it’s the little things that can make a big difference.
So he would give it a shot, and perhaps that would give him the push he needed.

"I can also use the sword dream now that my mind has become much stronger than before. I think I can handle the dreams, and perhaps, that will even give me the push I need to gain more enlightenment."
The sword tower had a lot to offer, so for now, he would turn to other things. But the moment he was done with his seclusion, he would have a lot to do before the apocalypse descends.
He didn’t want to jinx it, but he wanted the apocalypse to descend even faster.
He knew the Hand was doing their best to locate the Keys of the Apocalypse, but he was also working hard to ensure they met failure in whatever plans they were cooking up.
Kent rested for the day and then retrieved the next set of keys. He had two keys for his Chaos Dragon memories, so he quickly took out one.
"I guess this is it — time to meet the one who was known as the strongest being in all of existence — the wildcard who holds the key to end everything." Kent smiled.
"I wonder what I was like growing up."
Inside the Mountain Garden, the three lolis sighed, a smile playing on their lips.

⟪I guess this is it. We had a good run. The moment he retrieves his Dragon Lord memories, he will know all the pranks we played on him and punish us accordingly,⟫ Gaia said, and her two sisters nodded.
⟪Though these are just the first few years of his life, we are safe for now,⟫ Dori, being the mind of their group, offered her insight, and her sister sighed,
⟪We should be prepared either way.⟫
