chapters.title: Chapter 635: Meeting The Chaos Dragon [Bonus]
paragraphs: Sitting at the core of the universe, Lady Universe smiled when she saw what Kent was about to do.

"Looks like his destiny is about to take a turn. I wonder what he will do with what he was about to learn about his past." A smile appeared on her face. Suddenly, the enchantress’s voice entered her mind.

"You don’t have to worry about his mental health, sister; Doriana has that covered. The problem now is what he will do with the memories he is about to make, most importantly, what will happen to him after learning about his background."

Lady Universe smirked, "That is not our business—to worry about him. Like you said, he has Doriana. The question we should ask ourselves now is what will become of the universe when the Chaos Dragon is unleashed again."
The two ladies smiled.
They truly wanted to know because the Chaos Dragon was someone who had lived up to his name from the very beginning. He had no ordinary name, just one that described his nature.
"Oh Chaos, I wonder what you have planned for your future?"

Kent held the key for a few seconds before a smile appeared on his lips. "Time to meet myself, I guess." With that, he pressed the key against his forehead, and his consciousness was pulled into a realm.
Kent appeared in a serene forest, one with lush green plants and a beautiful, picturesque sky. The air smelled and tasted clean, and the wind blowing across the space was just too tantalizing.
Kent felt at home, like he was meant to be there. He immersed himself in the tranquil environment, even forgetting why he was there or what he was supposed to be doing at that moment.
"Beautiful, isn’t it?" Suddenly, a voice spoke, causing Kent to turn around and examine his environment. The moment he turned, his gaze met that of a handsome man.
The person had purple hair that flowed down his back, purple eyes, and deep golden dragon horns. He was clad in a simple tunic shirt and trousers that showed his perfect physique.
In his hand was an apple.
Kent observed him for a few seconds before a smirk appeared on his face.
"I guess the apple doesn’t fall far from the tree." The man who appeared before him smirked and threw an apple at him.
"Thanks," Kent said, accepting it.
Perhaps the apple doesn’t fall far from the tree, indeed. That was because the person who appeared was an exact copy of him.

While Jest bears a resemblance to him, the uncanny resemblance he shared with this man was strikingly similar to his current appearance. However, the man was more handsome, mature, and dangerous by all standards than he appeared to be.
However, they shared the same eye color and physical appearance.
"So you are the Chaos Dragon," Kent asked, biting into the apple.
"Indeed. You can call me Chaos," the man, who was identified as the Chaos Dragon, said.

"Chaos. Like, seriously. Don’t you have a normal dragon name, like Drogo or Drogan? Even Frodo is a good name... why only Chaos?" Kent asked, not understanding why someone would call themselves Chaos.
I mean, it sounded cool, but come on, that is just crazy.
Chaos looked at Kent and laughed. "You will understand later."
Kent sighed. "Though, aren’t you supposed to be dead or something? I mean, I didn’t meet Jest, so why am I meeting you? Not that I am complaining, but why?"
Chaos walked past Kent and then moved to a cliff not far from where they stood. Kent followed and stood beside him, looking like a father and son when in fact, they were the same person.
Chaos turned to him and smiled. Kent could swear he saw some emotions flash in those crazy purple eyes, but then they vanished.
"I reckon Jest is one of our incarnations?" he asked, and Kent nodded.
"Looks like it works. This is good." Chaos’s smile caused his eyes to flash golden for a second before returning to their purple form.

"To answer your question, I am here because of you. This consciousness is left in this realm, which is hidden deep within your mind. Now that you want to learn about your memories, I will guide you and perhaps answer your questions."

"This means if you have anything you want to know, I am ready to answer... Though you have to know I can’t answer all questions, the laws are not exactly deaf, you see." Chaos smiled, biting again into his apple. Kent did the same.
"First question, then. I want to know about how you died."
"Right off the bat, I see." Chaos smiled and then shook his head. "Unfortunately, I can’t tell you how I died."
"Why?" Kent asked, not liking how his first question had turned out. He knew the Chaos Dragon had died; he had learned that from Vexthra, so he wanted to know what had happened.

It all didn’t make any sense. The Chaos Dragon was the lone guardian to stay when the others were transcending.
He stood his ground and fought for what he loved, and died doing it. So if that was the case, why was he saying he never died?
Was it that he was mistaken for someone, or had he perhaps sustained brain damage during the battle? Kent looked at Chaos weirdly and then sighed.
"How are you still alive then, and what happened during the Great War?" he asked. That seemed like the logical question at the moment.
"The Great War, huh? Sounds like a good name, but I prepared for the Doom War. After all, it was then I died, yet I didn’t die.

You might think I am messing with you, but the truth of the matter is, I died, but I didn’t die. I died in the sense that my soul shattered, but I didn’t die because my soul never went to the underworld."

chapters.title: Chapter 636: Law of Creation [Bonus]
paragraphs: "This sounds more like a fantasy to me," Kent smirked. The underworld, where the soul travels, is not a place one could easily escape or refuse to go.
The moment you die, your soul will be ferried to that place. So, for Chaos to say his soul never went to that place, there has to be a reason.

Kent didn’t really expect the conversation to reach this stage, but he had to know, and from Chaos’s expression, it was clear he wanted to tell him because what he had to say was something Kent must understand early on in his journey to the top.
"I didn’t enter the underworld because I didn’t want to. And yes, I have the means to refuse death."
"How?" Kent asked.
"Because the reason why I was known as the greatest was due to something I achieved that, to this day, nobody has, and nobody else would be able to reach that... I touched the Dao of creation."
Kent looked at Chaos for a few minutes, then a big sigh escaped his lips. "This is the part where you tell me what the Dao of creation is."
Chaos laughed at what Kent had said. It sounded funny, but Kent was rather frustrated. It felt like he knew nothing, despite having already gone through Jest Memories for hundreds of years.

This also means that Jest doesn’t have memories of this, or he hasn’t yet reached that stage, which makes this conversation very important. He must know; he had to learn, and thus, Kent started to probe for information.
"It is simple, actually. I was the only one, and I am still sure I am the only one to master all seven primordial laws to perfection." Chaos looked at Kent with an amused expression.

"Life, Death, Time, Space, Void, Elemental, and Chaos. These are the seven laws of creation. All seven of these came together to form Creation. In other words, Creation came about due to these seven laws, and I master all of them."
Kent raised his brow, a shocked expression playing on his face.
’All seven laws of creation were mastered to perfection by him alone. That must have taken a very long time.’

"100 million years, to be exact," Chaos said, showing he could read Kent’s mind. Not that it wasn’t obvious, but Kent didn’t want to make a big deal out of it, so he looked at Chaos and asked a simple question.
"How was that possible?"
"It was very simple, really. I was challenged by someone to learn all seven primordial laws, and if I succeeded, they would grant me a special kind of reincarnation.
I know you will ask, but I can’t say who. However, you should know that this challenge wasn’t simple; it changed the fate of the universe we inhabit, and also the reason why we can never truly die.
It may appear in the history books that I died, but in reality, I didn’t. I created a different path, one where I disperse my existence in thirteen places."
Kent nodded with a thoughtful expression. "Why do such a thing? If I have the power of creation at my fingertips, why then do I have to go through all these troubles, leaving thirteen lives?
Why not just keep living the one life you had?"

Chaos smiled. "That is indeed a good question, Kent. But I can’t tell you why, though I can say sometimes, when you are at the end of your wits, you just have to look into the future and possibly timelines and wonder, what if I once had someone who could save me?"
Kent’s eyes widened, causing Chaos to smile.
Kent understood the reference, and it was something he learned the hard way. Vexthra had already spoken about the 14 legions that appeared during the great war.
She said they came from the future. And now, Chaos is talking about time and living thirteen lives. Linking the two makes perfect sense.
First, in a way, he might have found out the universe was dying or would die, and that was why he had to learn the law of creation.
This was because the laws of this universe are not that forgiving, and the only way to navigate them was to know them.
He had mastered creation, and so, even long before the war arrived, Chaos had already made his preparations.

And of course, this preparation didn’t happen in his present; it happened in his future, and the only way for him to be able to see that everything was in order was to ensure he was the one who formed this legion.
This means he had lived many lives that he created, and in these lives, his sole existence was to complete a task.
But if that was the case, does that mean his original existence was included in this task completion quest? Kent’s mind moved, forming all possible understanding he could derive from this.
’Thirteen lives, each with a purpose, each with a task. But why... I don’t understand.’
Chaos looked at Kent and smiled. Some things are not said out loud, and so Kent understood he can’t ask him.

This must be figured out on his own. The meaning behind his existence lay in his own hands. To understand what he had done during the primordial era, he must first ask himself some of the most important questions.
One being, how did he come to this conclusion that to save the past, the future must be secured?
But he already had an answer for that.
’The undead, the Lost Knights, the soul sentinels, and now, I have a feeling the dungeon bosses are also part of said legion.’

’This means all the 13 lives I led yielded one legion. Meaning in this life, I had yet to form a legion, the 14th legion, and somewhere in the future, I would be required to assemble all of them to face the Great War.’
’But if that is the case, then did this mean I will have to fight the Great War all over again?’ Kent asked himself, and the answer was rather funny.

’No. The concept of time is something I don’t understand, but if I know how the clock works, turning the hour hand back doesn’t mean it will remain in that position forever; it will eventually move forward to its original state.
Then this can only mean one thing.’
Kent turned and looked at Chaos, who already understood what was happening in Kent’s mind.
’This means time is not moving at all. It means somehow, I circled around time and did something that shouldn’t be possible, and now, I must pay for it...’
Kent broke into a cold sweat. ’This bastard.’

chapters.title: Chapter 637: What Did You Do? [Bonus]
paragraphs: "What did you do?" Kent asked, looking at Chaos as if he had made a blunder and needed to fix it.
"I can’t tell you that," Chaos replied with a nonchalant expression.
"Why?" Kent asked.
"If I tell you what happened, it wouldn’t happen," Chaos smirked, biting into his apple as he studied Kent’s expression.
A few seconds later, a smile appeared on his lips that caused Kent to wonder if he had indeed hit his head when he was a baby.

He had so many questions revolving around his understanding of what Chaos did. However, as it turned out, he had to give these questions to the passage of time, and eventually, if it pleased time, he would know the answers.
"I don’t even want to know anymore," Kent sighed and sat on the edge of the cliff, looking out at the humid expanse that spread far ahead of him.

Chaos also sat down and waved his hand. The moment he did, a thin line appeared before them. He snapped his fingers, and thirteen dots appeared on the line, each maintaining a certain distance from the others.
The distances varied, but they shared some likeness, such as the margin not being too broad.

"This was our lives. These thirteen dots are used to define our very existence. So far, you have claimed one part of it, and soon you will be claiming the second. However, before you do that, there is something else you must know."
Chaos waved his hand, and another line appeared. This time, however, there was only one dot. In the middle of these two lines, there was another line.
Though thin, it was there, and there was a small red dot in it, glowing eerily.
"What is that?" Kent asked.
"That is the real wildcard. It is a creation outside of time and space. That existence doesn’t have any rules binding it, and it is one we have lived before.

However, I don’t know what happened, and it was locked between the past and the future, outside of this timeline, yet within it. It is an existence we don’t have any recollection of... However, I found a way to get it."
Chaos snapped his finger, and a small red stone appeared. Kent had seen it before. "The Bloodheart Stone," he identified it.
"Indeed," Chaos nodded.

"To understand it all, claim all seven of these stones and absorb every last one of them. A day will come when you will be required to know everything. You must know that, when that day comes and the calling comes, don’t resist.
I did what I did because of this one sole existence, so be ready. Train hard, become the one who stands above all else, and hold your claim over everything.
Only then will you be ready to know what happened and why I went through all this trouble for our future."
"I understand," Kent nodded. He had already acquired one Bloodheart Stone that he would absorb after he was done with everything. Now, he understood that he must get all seven.
"When will I become a full Dragon?" Kent chose to go back to the basics. All this talk about what happened billions of years ago tired his brain.
"The Chaos Dragon bloodline is a powerful one. So for now, don’t think about when you will become a full dragon; worry about how you will handle your awakening."
"What do you mean?" Kent asked, not liking the direction this was taking. He wanted to become a dragon, but how was that now turning into an awakening?
But Chaos shook his head,

"Just messing with you. However, to take your complete dragon form, you must first unlock Dragon Claws, Dragon Wings, Dragon Scales, Dragon Tail, Dragon Horns, Dragon Aura, Dragon Presence, and Dragon Breath.
These are the basic concepts. Of course, the majority are in your blood, so it is only a matter of time. However, if you are in a hurry to become a dragon, there are three ways.
The first is to review all my memories. And let me tell you, I led a very long and adventurous life...so it will be a while.

The second is that you must find a place rich in Chaos Energy and train there. This will hasten your bloodline awakening. Your bloodline is Chaos energy, so training in a Chaos-rich area is perfect for you.
I recommend this method because it not only hastens the process but also improves your combat prowess.
If you can even start comprehending the laws of chaos, I am sure you will begin slaying immortals long before you become one.
As for the third, you just have to hunt creatures that have Chaos affinity. After killing them, you can absorb their blood essence, which will hasten your growth.
However, I must warn you that doing this will introduce a new aspect to your bloodline that I do not recommend.
Dragon Bloodlust shouldn’t be taken lightly, so unless your grip on the law of death is firm, don’t attempt this third method."
Kent nodded at Chaos’s words. He already suspected his bloodline would see some advancement after reviewing the memories. So this was already enough for him.
"One last question," Kent said, noticing his consciousness start to turn hazy. "Is the Primordial Era still out there? I mean, are there like fragments out there?"

From Jest’s memories, he learned of some rumors that suggested the Primordial Era is still there, lost in space. Of course, they were just rumors. But now that he was talking to someone who lived in said era, he had to ask.
"The ruins of my era are still there... Though I have to warn you, entering said places is dangerous, so be careful when you enter one."
"Aren’t you going to tell me not to enter one?" Kent laughed, and Chaos also couldn’t help smirking.

"Knowing you—knowing us—we will be the first to jump in, so my advice is for you to be prepared and don’t be careless." He paused and then added, "Even if you don’t cherish your life, know that there are others out there depending on you, even if you don’t know they exist."
"One last thing: your name is Kent, not Chaos, so limit the destruction you cause," Chaos said with one last laugh.
With that, Kent’s consciousness vanished and entered the first memory.
It was time for him to know about the Chaos Dragon, the one that came into existence through Chaos and Destruction.

"One last question," Kent said, noticing his consciousness start to turn hazy.
"Is the Primordial Era still out there?
I mean, are there like fragments out there?"
From Jest’s memories, he learned of some rumors that suggested the Primordial Era is still there, lost in space.
Of course, they were just rumors.
But now that he was talking to someone who lived in said era, he had to ask.
"The ruins of my era are still there...
Though I have to warn you, entering said places is dangerous, so be careful when you enter one."
"Aren’t you going to tell me not to enter one?" Kent laughed, and Chaos also couldn’t help smirking.

"Knowing you—knowing us—we will be the first to jump in, so my advice is for you to be prepared and don’t be careless." He paused and then added, "Even if you don’t cherish your life, know that there are others out there depending on you, even if you don’t know they exist."
"One last thing: your name is Kent, not Chaos, so limit the destruction you cause," Chaos said with one last laugh.
With that, Kent’s consciousness vanished and entered the first memory.
It was time for him to know about the Chaos Dragon, the one that came into existence through Chaos and Destruction.

chapters.title: Chapter 638: The Primordial Chaos Dragon [Bonus]
paragraphs: Chaos was a name that, from the start of his life, was all about being Chaotic.
He was a child born without parents. He was born into the chaotic world of Lumen, a rather sinister place that had ever existed during the primordial era.
Lumen, as they called it, was the kind of place the scum of society loved... and Chaos was one such scum, from the moment he was born—well, hatched.
From the moment he opened his eyes, he never knew peace—a young dragon with nothing but his wit pushing him.
Dragons from Lumen are known as natural predators, and Chaos quickly picked up this nature, the predatory nature.
Chaos grew up learning how to survive from one night to the next and how to make the next move to secure the next day.
He never dreamed of what he would eat in the next two days or the week ahead. His dream was always about what to eat today and what to eat tomorrow.
Thinking too far ahead was but an unrealistic dream to Chaos. He didn’t believe he could live that long to see that day. So the farthest dream he could dream was 24 hours ahead.
And that was his life, and Lumen was his only place to keep his head. He liked it there regardless. He had friends—other scum who would do anything for food.
However, was Lumen really this hard? Was it meant to be this hard?
The answer is no. The reason Lumen was a challenging place to love was due to the three great families who never stopped fighting over resources.
They are the cause of everything wrong with Lumen, and people like Chaos were left to bear the hard life, for that was what they were created for.
By 17, Chaos had lost more friends than he could count. Every friend he lost was a stark reminder of how worthless life is.
But as a Chaos Dragon, Chaos never truly believed his life was worthless. No, Chaos believed his destiny was to lay waste to the three great families, so that was what he did.

A creature born out of chaos is meant to bring chaos to everyone. He knew his life had purpose, and to realize that life, to be able to dream and see his life more than 24 hours ahead, he knew he had to become who he was meant to be.
So Chaos jumped into the Primal Void, the only place the three Great Families couldn’t control; it was also a place only Chaos could enter without difficulty, for that was where he was born.

Nobody knew what was in there, and nobody wanted to find out; after all, millions who had gone in thousands of years before had yet to return. So when Chaos said he would be back, his words were but a joke to many.
Until he returned, 30 years later.
The day he returned was the day of reckoning for the three great families.
Chaos entered the Primal Void as a mortal dragon and returned as a Chaos Dragon with powers none of the people in Lumen could comprehend.
He was able to influence the very air around him, turning calmness chaotic and making life as chaotic as it could be. His mere presence was disorganized, and his absence was even more chaotic.
Wherever his name was mentioned, chaos erupted, and whenever his presence was felt, it never washed away.
In the end, Lumen became the Lumen that most immortals sought to visit, to gain insight into an existence whose mere name could bring tyrants to their knees years later.
Kent opened his eyes, feeling the air around him turn chaotic. His body was reacting to it, and while he never honestly asked for it, his form had changed into that of a demi-dragon.
The air shifted, twisting with its chaotic essence for a few hours before it came to a stop. By then, Kent felt his body undergo some changes that left him in awe of what had just happened to him.
"This feeling is great; it is like I can stand against anything and have no fear." His blood was boiling, and the madness that came with it was influencing him.
"No wonder Chaos was that mad. To stand against three such powerful families and smile at them, I have to say, he had some spine," Kent chuckled.
He saw how Chaos came about. His birth was never truly understood, but his life had been a harsh one. However, he learned from it, adapted, and made his resolve when he lost too much.
So he understood where the madness was coming from, and as someone who had the Chaotic Bloodline that once brought immortals and gods to their knees, Kent understood he was no simple person.
"However, there is a problem here," Kent sighed.

"I need to find a way to temper my bones with chaotic essence. Chaos had the Primal Expanse for that. But I don’t, and while using pressure can do that, I need to get the real thing. That is the only way I can realize my potential as a Chaos Dragon."
Chaos didn’t use any weapons; he was a body cultivator, and as such, he had become powerful by tempering his body and bones.

Kent had already started tempering his body; it was left with his bones, and while the Titan Stairway had given him elixirs that had started tempering his bones, now that he had awakened Chaos’s memories, he knew he wasn’t doing much.
The best part was that he had the Chaos bloodline, which would slowly temper his bones as he awakened it. Talking about his bloodline, Kent checked the messages he had received.
⟦Congratulations, you have awakened 13% of your Primordial Chaos Dragon Bloodline⟧
"There were no new aspects, but I can move two times faster than when it was just 10% awakened. Also, my claws have become much stronger, and my scales make my defense even harder.

I guess I didn’t run out of luck getting the first memories out of the way. Now, I need to check the second." Kent used the key, but to his shock, a golden diary appeared, showing he was ready for his first Dragonic Enlightenment.
He opened it and started to read.

chapters.title: Chapter 639: Chaos Journey [Bonus]
paragraphs: [So I killed the last of the three great families today, and it felt nice. At long last, they won’t be able to cause any more damage to anyone.
However, I now find myself in a difficult situation. That old bastard. It turns out that killing the three great families was a bad thing in some way.
I discovered that Lumen is home to a rare type of mineral called Spirit Stones. These spirit stones contain spiritual energy that most cultivators utilize to enhance their cultivation bases.
Not that I need it...
For centuries, the three great families have been fighting over it, hence the chaos that we, the commoners, have had to endure.
However, aside from their battles, they were also the force that prevented others from invading.
It turns out that the only three gateways to Lumen were protected by a powerful formation that, from that old bastard’s mouth, not even immortals could break.
But now that I have killed them, it will only be a matter of time before those outside Lumen find out and invade. When that happens, I will be powerless to stop them.]
"Aah, what a dumbass," Kent smirked, flipping to the next page of the diary. However, when he read the first line, his back broke into a sweat.
"He is crazy, totally crazy."
[Actually, I wanted them to invade. I want them to come so I can start cultivating this damn technique the Leviathan gave me when I visited the Primal Void.
I need the blood, loads of blood, and since they are serving themselves on a silver platter, who am I to reject?

The Primal Bone Tempering Art requires me to slaughter as many idiots as I can to temper my bones. I know it is sinister, but that is the only way I can live up to the contract I made with the Leviathan.
So I have to bide my time and wait for the invaders to come.]

"Crazy," Kent took a deep breath, feeling the craziness seep into his bones. The fact that someone who was only a spirit king was waiting for possible immortals was enough for him to realize how crazy he had been in the past.
"However, the Primal Bone Tempering Art is what I need right now.
It will not only enhance my body and bones, but it will also make me a predator, someone worthy of once being the opponent of the infamous Abyssal Leviathan, the overlord of the wild."
Kent laughed, feeling the craziness stir within him.
Inside the Mountain Garden, Dori and her sister were watching their master with smiles on their faces.
⟪I can start to see that craziness surface. Mercy on the souls of those who would anger him. I fear for them,⟫ Gaia said, shaking her small head. Her sisters were the same.
⟪His bloodline is already thirteen percent, yet that craziness has started to surface. Makes me wonder, would this version of him become even crazier?⟫ Akira asked.
⟪Only natural. He has lived many lives after all, and while I won’t say all of them were crazy like the Chaos Dragon era, he was a menace in all, so it is only normal.
The question, however, should be whether he can control the chaos and not exacerbate it, as he did in Lumen.⟫
The three sisters nodded, looked at each other, and sighed in unison.
Kent flipped to the next page of the diary.

[So I killed 12 thousand people today. Although I couldn’t reach all of them, the 12,000 are from a world called Myrrath. I don’t know where it is located, but I believe they are demons who can breathe fire.
Makes me sad I can’t do that despite being a dragon. However, I learned something new... Killing is so much fun.]
Kent’s eyes remained on the book, looking at the words written in black, and he just couldn’t fathom how someone could be this crazy.
"At this point, I think we were crazy — I was crazy. But strangely, it felt good slaughtering them. After all, they came to destroy my world, and I wouldn’t let that happen.
All those who cross me will die."
Kent’s eyes turned golden, and the aura of chaos radiated from him. Without even knowing it, his claws were activated as he said those words. However, a few seconds later, a sigh escaped his lips.
"I was a menace. However, while I understand what I did, perhaps I could have been more welcoming and not gone straight to slaughter." He smiled, then continued to read.
[Okay. So the slaughter I committed wasn’t in vain. I managed to comprehend the first form of The Primal Bone Tempering Art.
This made my claws three times stronger, and my Dragon Aura now has that primal kink to it. I think I am becoming a predator, and the feeling is incredible.
However, I also think I may have gone overboard the last time. Perhaps I will be more civil next time and try to make things more peaceful.
However, the people of Lumen are happy with my leadership. Life is good, and while the slaughter is too much, they seem not to care.
Perhaps they are too afraid to say anything, considering on occasion I hear whispers of people saying I am a tyrant. Not that I care.
I don’t need their praise anyway. The only thing I need now is to grow stronger and have my battle with Leviathan.]
Kent flipped to the next page.
[So the civil approach didn’t work, so I had to lay waste to a thousand more. This time, they put up a fight. However, they couldn’t break past me.
Also, I managed to get one of their boats, which can travel through the spatial channels.
I am considering leaving Lumen to give them an in-person warning. However, I am afraid they will come while I am gone, so for now, I am weighing my options.
On one side, I could wait for the strongest of them to come, then after I kill all of them, I can travel to nearby worlds and give them a stern warning.
Or I can risk it and go bananas.]

chapters.title: Chapter 640: First Human Friend [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Ah, it turns out people can be civil after all. So, all the slaughter could have been avoided if those demons had just been civil.
It has already been three years since the last slaughter. However, I spent the best part of those three years training in the Damned Forest. It was a good place for dragons like me.
I became a Level 3 Spirit King just a few months ago, but it turns out that before I can become a Spirit Emperor and Sovereign, I must comprehend the third form of the Primal Bone Tempering Art.
Laviathan said nothing about that. But I need to prepare some ingredients first, but I can’t find all of them in Lumen. So I need to go outside after all.
The only problem is that I don’t know anywhere aside from Lumen, and even though I have a boat that can travel the vast expanse of void space, I still lack a destination.
So for now, I will bide my time and wait for the next invaders.]

Kent sighed. He didn’t even want to turn to the next page in fear that he would see another slaughter. He was indeed a menace, and that was why he never honestly told himself much, but only warned himself to tone it down a bit.
"But to think I broke three limits already, I guess I am qualified to kill Spirit Lords and soon even a Heavenly Ascension expert."
From the memories, it turns out the Primal Bone Tempering Art is meant to break limits in his bones and body.
There are many limits on every aspect of a being. There are limits on the mind, soul, body, and cultivation path, and perhaps others as well.
So far, Kent has broken one limit on his body and another on his cultivation. However, Chaos broke three limits on his body.
That makes him someone very dangerous, and if he manages to cultivate the technique to all seven levels, who knows how many limits he will break.
If three limits were broken after comprehending two levels of a technique, then what happens when all seven are comprehended?
Kent knew he had to review that, so he dug back into the diary.
[So I found an old map from the rubble of the three great families. It turns out that Lumen is part of the Lanky Planetary Alliance, which consists of seven worlds.
In the past, the Myrrath and Serraxis tried to evade Lumen, but the three great families held them back. I think Myrrath were those idiots I killed.
They were much more pressing than Serraxis, who I read are humans. Lumen is a beast world, so hearing about humans who are known to fancy taming beasts like me is something I am looking forward to.
This means more slaughter if that is the only way to let them know Lumen is out of reach. Of course, if they turn out not to be like the demons, I will have a civil talk with them.]
"I guess I could use some humanity after all." Kent smiled as he flipped to the next page.
[So it turns out the humans are scum, and I had to kill yet again. However, I only killed 99 and let one live. She tried to stop her people when they attacked me, while I tried to be civil.
I mean, why should I even bother being civil? Killing without any question or warning sounds like the best thing for me. However, today I saw humans aren’t all that bad in a way.
Her name is Elina, a Spirit Sovereign and a swordsman. I mistakenly struck her with my tail, and she passed out, so I took her to the healers after slaughtering her cohort.

It is only fair that they pay for attempting to take what didn’t belong to them. Those idiots nearly made me lower my guard, which would have been fatal if Elina, their leader, wasn’t a good person — I think.
She can play me, but I will squeeze the life out of her before she even has the chance to do anything.]
"Ha," Kent sighed, then a smile appeared on his face.

"He is not wrong, or more like I was not wrong. Humans... some of them are scum. Even in a place like Earth, humans can willingly type in their passcode and unleash nuclear weapons on their fellow humans.
They are indeed scum."
[So Elina woke up, and we had a nice talk. It turns out she is the daughter of a powerful merchant who holds a relatively high position in Serraxis.
The Emperor of Serraxis sent her and her team to negotiate a peaceful deal with Lumen after hearing about what happened to Myrrath when they tried to evade.
As the daughter of a merchant and also a good swordsman, they added her as the leader of the negotiation. Basically, their job was to establish peaceful contact with Lumen, in this case, me.
However, her teammates saw me as a weakling, and so when they found out I am the leader of the Lumen beast race, they tried to eliminate me.
She did not hate me for killing her teammates, though I think she is scared of me.]
"Dumbass, can’t you see how she was fidgeting with her fingers while talking to you? Do you even look at yourself in the mirror?" Kent laughed.
The audacity he had to write something that obvious. However, turning to the last page, he smiled.

[So I decided to let Elina go. She promised to come back a year later with some good news and even the ingredients for the tempering, so I can finally step into the third stage in The Primal Bone Tempering Art

I’m not sure if I can trust her. However, I am nearing a stage in my Claw Arts that will raise my battle prowess to a new level. If she turns out to be scum too, I will happily tear her apart like a rag.

Thankfully, that didn’t happen. A year and a half later, Elina came with seven people now. All were important people of her race, and this time, they came to negotiate a deal that would benefit both Serraxis and Lumen.
Also, Elina and I became friends, my first human friend who promised to take me around the world... I think I can trust her.]
Kent closed the diary, which had the name "Chaos Diary 1/99" on it. However, the moment he closed the diary, it turned into sparks and entered his forehead.
Thus, his first Dragonic Enlightenment was underway...

This means more slaughter if that is the only way to let them know Lumen is out of reach.
Of course, if they turn out not to be like the demons, I will have a civil talk with them.]
"I guess I could use some humanity after all." Kent smiled as he flipped to the next page.
[So it turns out the humans are scum, and I had to kill yet again.
However, I only killed 99 and let one live.
She tried to stop her people when they attacked me, while I tried to be civil.
I mean, why should I even bother being civil?
Killing without any question or warning sounds like the best thing for me.
However, today I saw humans aren’t all that bad in a way.
Her name is Elina, a Spirit Sovereign and a swordsman.
I mistakenly struck her with my tail, and she passed out, so I took her to the healers after slaughtering her cohort.
It is only fair that they pay for attempting to take what didn’t belong to them.
Those idiots nearly made me lower my guard, which would have been fatal if Elina, their leader, wasn’t a good person — I think.
She can play me, but I will squeeze the life out of her before she even has the chance to do anything.]
"Ha," Kent sighed, then a smile appeared on his face.
"He is not wrong, or more like I was not wrong.
Humans... some of them are scum.
Even in a place like Earth, humans can willingly type in their passcode and unleash nuclear weapons on their fellow humans.
They are indeed scum."
[So Elina woke up, and we had a nice talk.
It turns out she is the daughter of a powerful merchant who holds a relatively high position in Serraxis.
The Emperor of Serraxis sent her and her team to negotiate a peaceful deal with Lumen after hearing about what happened to Myrrath when they tried to evade.
As the daughter of a merchant and also a good swordsman, they added her as the leader of the negotiation.
Basically, their job was to establish peaceful contact with Lumen, in this case, me.
However, her teammates saw me as a weakling, and so when they found out I am the leader of the Lumen beast race, they tried to eliminate me.
She did not hate me for killing her teammates, though I think she is scared of me.]
"Dumbass, can’t you see how she was fidgeting with her fingers while talking to you?
Do you even look at yourself in the mirror?" Kent laughed.
The audacity he had to write something that obvious.
However, turning to the last page, he smiled.
[So I decided to let Elina go.
She promised to come back a year later with some good news and even the ingredients for the tempering, so I can finally step into the third stage in The Primal Bone Tempering Art
I’m not sure if I can trust her.
However, I am nearing a stage in my Claw Arts that will raise my battle prowess to a new level.
If she turns out to be scum too, I will happily tear her apart like a rag.
Thankfully, that didn’t happen.
A year and a half later, Elina came with seven people now.
All were important people of her race, and this time, they came to negotiate a deal that would benefit both Serraxis and Lumen.
Also, Elina and I became friends, my first human friend who promised to take me around the world...
I think I can trust her.]
Kent closed the diary, which had the name "Chaos Diary 1/99" on it.
However, the moment he closed the diary, it turned into sparks and entered his forehead.
Thus, his first Dragonic Enlightenment was underway...

chapters.title: Chapter 641: The Primal Bone Tempering Art & Claw Art [Bonus]
paragraphs: The Enlightenment was long but rewarding.

Kent lasted ten good years in that enlightenment. This indicates that he made significant progress during the Enlightenment. In most cases, spending a prolonged period in an enlightened state proves beneficial.
Kent spent ten years in there, and the outcome was as he had expected.
⟦Congratulations, you have awakened 16% of your Primordial Chaos Dragon Bloodline⟧
[You have awakened Chaos Claw Aura]
⟦Name: Chaos Claw Aura⟧
⟦Mastery: Beginner⟧
⟦Description: Coat your Dragon claws with Chaos energy that significantly enhances your battle power. The higher your mastery, the stronger the effect⟧
This was the first gift he received after the enlightenment. It isn’t that fancy, but as a dragon, this was an ability he would cherish for years to come.
The fact that he can coat his claws with Chaos energy was enough to show he can fight like a dragon in his demi-dragon form. Kent would be someone to be feared.
"In Chaos memories, he had mastered this to the second stage, which is the Proficient stage. This means that if I reach that level, my claw will be seven times stronger.

Even now, it is already on a level I don’t think a Spirit King can take. I’d better practice more of the Claw Art, then." Kent tapped into the technique, and his mind, as usual, was pulled into a realm where he could practice.
This space was a wasteland, with shattered mountains and twisted, dead trees all around. It was always different for different techniques, so this dead wasteland was the one for the Claw Art.
A few seconds after he appeared, a large dragon emerged, bringing a powerful presence to the area. The dragon was so large that Kent had to take several steps back.
If he weren’t underestimating the dragon, he would say it was about 100 km long, and that isn’t something small to even start to think about.
Suddenly, the dragon raised his right claw and took a mighty swing. This caused three powerful dark gold arcs to appear and strike the very ground Kent was standing on.
A power explosion occurred that forced lava from the ground, and before Kent knew it, his consciousness was forced out of the Mind realm, causing him to break into a cold sweat.
"What the hell was that?" Kent’s breath turned ragged as he tried to calm his mind, though he wasn’t having much success in that department. However, the feeling of great primal fear washed over him.
"Dori, any explanations?" Kent asked. The feeling he received could have killed him or meant to kill him. It was strange but fearful.

⟪What the master experienced is called technique Intent. All techniques have different skills. So, although the Claw Art has the same skill throughout, it has levels, and the first level involves three arcs being unleashed from the swing.
What you felt was the intent of the first level of the Claw Art. It is essentially the intent that determines who qualifies to master the Claw Art⟫.
"So, does it mean I am not destined to learn this technique?"
⟪No, master. It has nothing to do with destiny. You can learn it; any dragon or clawed-type beast can learn it. But before you can do that, you first must withstand the intent.
Your mind and soul must be strong enough to withstand the intent. Only after that can you learn the technique. Before you ask, yes, all seven levels require you to withstand the intent.
So, for now, let it be. Your soul is strong; that’s why you didn’t pass out. However, your mind is still lacking, so work on that before attempting again⟫
"I understand," Kent sighed and then chose to heed Dori’s advice. Not that he needed to heed anyone’s advice. The danger he felt from the skill was just too much for him to handle.
"In the end, it turns out Chaos is much more impressive than I. It wasn’t obvious; dude practically lived a gladiator life, so his mindset is much stronger than mine.

However, I also have something he doesn’t have, and that is a tower that will make me grow stronger faster, so I guess I need to train harder, and the time to learn this technique will come soon enough."
"As for the Primal Bone Tempering Art, I just need to kill a lot to cultivate it," Kent smiled. "Good thing I have the dungeons and the Orc Alliance waiting for me to slaughter."

Though he needed to keep things civil most of the time, he knew slaughter was also a way to do things. Chaos tried to be civil, and he was nearly stabbed in the back, so when it calls for it, he will do what is required at that moment.
"But I should probably use that technique much faster. Being able to fight in my demi-dragon form seems to have some kink to it. Perhaps, being a swordsman and a dragon is good."
After checking his gains from the Enlightenment, Kent decided to turn his attention to the last memory key.

This one was meant to awaken memories of his life as the infamous faceless assassin. He was rather excited about this memory because he wanted to learn how someone could live for thousands of years, yet nobody knew his true appearance.
"Was that even possible? I mean, to live without a face." Kent was eager to find out. After all, it was his life, and as such, he must find out who he was.
He pressed the key against his forehead, and his consciousness was pulled into yet another realm that made him wonder why Jest never had that.
He was about to meet the realm’s faceless assassin.
Lady Universe sighed, a smile playing on her lips. "Looks like he wouldn’t be that crazy after all."
"I think so too. However, he has now started to awaken his memories, so I doubt it will remain like that forever," the Enchantress responded.
"Well, that would be for the future to determine. But until then, we can only hope he doesn’t make things much more chaotic than they already are." Lady Universe smiled.
"Ahh, what a headache. How can a single existence make us all stand on edge?" the Enchantress smirked, saying that.
"What can I say? He is the Chaos Dragon after all."

chapters.title: Chapter 642: The Faceless Assassin [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent appeared in a rather bizarre place.
When his consciousness was pulled away, he found himself in front of an old castle. It was old, considering the worn-out walls and wood. Crows circled it as if it were some ritual ground.
Creak.
Suddenly, the large door creaked open, and a voice came from inside, causing Kent to wonder if he should be there in the first place.
"You’re not going to keep standing there, are you?"
Kent gave the castle a curious look for a few more seconds before walking inside. Surprisingly, the interior wasn’t that eerie. However, it wasn’t without its wonders and some terrific displays.
On one side of the large hall where he appeared, a young man stood, cleaning a stained dagger. Lying on the table were thousands of different weapons that had been polished to their finest.
"First rule of an assassin, always treat your weapons like you treat yourself," the man behind the table said, focusing on the dagger for a couple of minutes before turning to Kent.
"You arrived earlier than I expected... So why don’t we change location?" With that, Kent found himself standing on a large bridge made out of bone.

Perhaps that was how he saw it, or how it looked, but the bone was colossal and formed into a bridge. The river below had black water, and even from the bridge, Kent could tell that many hungry monsters were hidden within.
Kent focused his attention on the man beside him.
Although this person had short, dark hair and handsome features, he paled in comparison to Chaos’s handsomeness.

It was just that he didn’t look too eerie, similar to Kent. However, comparing him to other people didn’t suit him either, because while he stood with Kent, Kent could have sworn the man didn’t have one face.
It was like when he blinked, a new face stared at him. However, he also understood that every face somehow resembled his own.
"You tell me when you are done," the man said with a smile.
"Go ahead, what is your name and your true face?" Kent asked, getting straight to the point. If this man was supposed to be his past, the least he could do was show him his face.
"I remember my name, but I forgot how I look. Of course, you will soon find out my actual appearance, considering you will be going down memory lane soon enough.
But for now, you can call me Faceless."
"And it gets weirder by the second," Kent sighed. Having just finished retrieving a part of Chaos’ memories, being asked to be called Faceless by a new version of himself didn’t sound too bad.
After all, he had already accepted the fact that his incarnations would have weirder names.
"So, Faceless, why am I here?" Kent asked.
"How would I know? You’re the one who came here, so why don’t you tell me why you’re here?" Faceless looked at Kent for a few seconds before a smirk appeared on his face.
"Just messing with you. The reason you’re here is that I have something to show you." Faceless looked down, staring at the black water as if there was something hidden inside.
"This is the Sea of Darkness. It is one of the oldest seas in the universe, and hidden deep inside is the gate to the Lost Realm. Some famous swordsman left it...
I have never been there before, but from what I know, the hidden races are there and looking for a way back.
Of course, not all of them deserve to be back. But most are to be brought back, for they will be needed. Again, don’t ask me what they will be required for because I don’t know."

"I understand. I will stay away from there," Kent nodded with a thoughtful expression. He didn’t want to show it, but he had a nagging feeling that nothing good would ever come of it—and he was right.
"That is the thing, because of me, you will have to go there," Faceless said, and Kent’s brow furrowed.
"Why?" he asked.
"Because you have to, else you will die," Faceless replied with a smile.
"Why again?" Kent asked.
"Because to get where you want to go—where we want to go—we must first get to the Lost Realm. That is the only way, and while I would love to say there is another way, there isn’t.
Trust me, I have looked, and the only thing I found was nothing. So I brought you here to show you this because it isn’t in my memories.
That will be all."
Kent nodded. He already had a lot of things to do, so adding one more wouldn’t be too much of an ask.
"Where can I find it?"
"I don’t know. And before you raise your brow, know that I truly don’t know, so don’t bother asking me. But I do know this: the Lost Realm will seek you when you are ready.
Somehow, you will know where to go when the time is right. So just prepare and be ready. That is all I can say.
Aside from that, though, I must warn you: learning the Faceless Art is not something to be taken for granted.
It is one of the most profound Arts in existence, and taking it as a joke will cost you. It has the potential to do so much good, but also to bring calamity.
So, if you’re not ready, don’t indulge in it. Also, never forget how you look... I made that mistake, and it cost me so much that I sometimes get lost in the thrill of the hunt."
Kent sighed inwardly as his consciousness began to drift away. He was nearing the end of his stay in the realm he was in. "One last question... what can you tell me of the Midnight Shadows?"
Faceless smiled at Kent, then chuckled. "You can trust them, but you must be careful... they are some of the most dangerous assassins in the universe."
With that, Kent vanished into the first memory he had of Faceless.

chapters.title: Chapter 643: The One Without a Face [Bonus]
paragraphs: Jaqen was his name—a name spoken only once and never to be heard again. His mother was the only one to call him that, and she died a few minutes after.
So his name was lost to time, and so was his face.
Jaqen was a child born of the union between an assassin and her target. He was never meant to exist in the first place. Thus, his name was never mentioned again.
When his mother chose to fall in love instead of kill, his fate was sealed. His destiny was written, and his life was marked with a number.
They called him Seventeen, the one who was to die when he turned seventeen. His blood was meant to serve as the awakening ritual to appease the immortals.
The Shadows were those who killed his mother and chose him to be used as a lamb for sacrifice. His destiny was written, and so was theirs.
What nobody realized was that Jaqen was no normal person, and that planning his life to the end was their own mistake.

The Faceless Art was a gift left behind by his mother, said to awaken when he turned sixteen. However, it changed his appearance long before the Shadows found him. His face was only known to his mother.

So he accepted his birthright at sixteen, and when he was seventeen, he killed the first thousand people. His life was meant to end when he turned seventeen, but by then, he had ended a thousand lives.
And that was when he lost his identity. The first person he killed was a guard. Then the guard killed the leader of all the guards.
The leader then killed one elder of the Shadows, one of the notorious assassination organizations in Klipton. They were the deadliest of all assassins.
Kings, emperors, and monarchs feared them. They were untouchable.
However, they fell because of a seventeen-year-old boy who had too much anger bottled up, and despite not having the means to kill, he managed somehow to end their lives, learning as he did it.

The elder killed the grand elder, and the grand elder killed the second general, who also went ahead and killed the first general before Lord Assassin himself found himself staring at his headless body.
By the time he was done, he forgot how he looked when he started killing. It was the most bizarre thing, but he accepted his reality, and that was when—or how—the Faceless Assassin was unleashed.
He had no recollection of how he looked, but he accepted himself, and however he looked, he made it his own.
Kent opened his eyes with a calm look on his face.
"This is crazy," he muttered, looking at the sky.
What he had just seen was a person who takes on the face of those he killed and lives their life perfectly. He was an actor, someone who could portray someone else’s life as if it were an act.
His perfection was too flawless ever to doubt. He played his role perfectly, and in the end, he managed to kill even a Root Immortal whole, only at the Spirit Ascension stage.
"I need to break his record. I must kill an immortal before I reach the Spirit Ascension stage," Kent smiled. Of all he saw in Faceless’s memories, he was a very meticulous person.
He killed most of his targets from several miles away.
"He was one terrifying accident creator. He is good, and that was just the first forty-five years of his life." Kent nodded with a satisfied expression.
He never truly understood how some of the kills occurred, but every time Faceless used his brain to kill, it was always successful.
"I was awesome," Kent laughed. He was very proud of himself. Not that it wasn’t weird—it was strange—but it was his life, so he could live it however he wanted.
He sighed and then accessed the Faceless Art.
It was a straightforward technique that offered numerous benefits. First, aside from being able to change his face, he could also alter his voice and even modify his body shape.
It was just like the Perfect Disguise skill Vexthra gave Kent.
However, this one copied the person’s memories and, to some extent, suppressed the user’s memories almost to the point that if they remained in their new persona, they would forget their true self.
It was one terrifying skill that made Kent wonder where his mother had gotten it from. But in the end, he learned it. He knew it would come in handy somehow.
He wasn’t planning on becoming the Faceless Assassin. However, he was also not about to discard such a powerful technique.
He knew it would come in handy one of these days.
"Now, the only thing left for me to do is find a way to get to the immortal worlds so I can kill an immortal and make Faceless’s record obsolete."

He laughed and then lay down, deciding to catch some rest before returning to his training. It had already been over twenty years since he entered seclusion, and during that time, a great deal had happened.

First, the humans in the tower were all thriving. They were all powerful cultivators now. Fifteen years ago, Akira ensured that they all underwent a ritual in which she bestowed upon them some powerful classes.
This was something Kent told her to do. Afterward, they underwent rigorous training that gradually elevated them to the top, much like the warriors they were meant to be.
Gaia wanted to ensure that the first humans in the tower would one day become beings capable of handling the many races her master would add. She spared no expense helping them.
Now, they were all training in and out of the dungeons. As for the Bloodvein Tribe, they were now more monstrous than before.
The tribe chief had raised his chaos affinity to the Perfect stage. Over the last twenty years, he had undergone two additional evolutions, placing him at the pinnacle of the core formation stage.
Gaia gave him a treasure to strengthen his foundation. This, of course, involved training inside the dungeons, and as a race known for war and killing, he had improved tremendously.
But he wasn’t the only one. Hundreds of Bloodvein warriors were growing at a speed many kingdoms would fear.
Then came Kent’s harem.

sentences.text: Jaqen was his name—a name spoken only once and never to be heard again.
His mother was the only one to call him that, and she died a few minutes after.
So his name was lost to time, and so was his face.
Jaqen was a child born of the union between an assassin and her target.
He was never meant to exist in the first place.
Thus, his name was never mentioned again.
When his mother chose to fall in love instead of kill, his fate was sealed.
His destiny was written, and his life was marked with a number.
They called him Seventeen, the one who was to die when he turned seventeen.
His blood was meant to serve as the awakening ritual to appease the immortals.
The Shadows were those who killed his mother and chose him to be used as a lamb for sacrifice.
His destiny was written, and so was theirs.
What nobody realized was that Jaqen was no normal person, and that planning his life to the end was their own mistake.
The Faceless Art was a gift left behind by his mother, said to awaken when he turned sixteen.
However, it changed his appearance long before the Shadows found him.
His face was only known to his mother.
So he accepted his birthright at sixteen, and when he was seventeen, he killed the first thousand people.
His life was meant to end when he turned seventeen, but by then, he had ended a thousand lives.
And that was when he lost his identity.
The first person he killed was a guard.
Then the guard killed the leader of all the guards.
The leader then killed one elder of the Shadows, one of the notorious assassination organizations in Klipton.
They were the deadliest of all assassins.
Kings, emperors, and monarchs feared them.
They were untouchable.
However, they fell because of a seventeen-year-old boy who had too much anger bottled up, and despite not having the means to kill, he managed somehow to end their lives, learning as he did it.

The elder killed the grand elder, and the grand elder killed the second general, who also went ahead and killed the first general before Lord Assassin himself found himself staring at his headless body.
By the time he was done, he forgot how he looked when he started killing.
It was the most bizarre thing, but he accepted his reality, and that was when—or how—the Faceless Assassin was unleashed.
He had no recollection of how he looked, but he accepted himself, and however he looked, he made it his own.
Kent opened his eyes with a calm look on his face.
"This is crazy," he muttered, looking at the sky.
What he had just seen was a person who takes on the face of those he killed and lives their life perfectly.
He was an actor, someone who could portray someone else’s life as if it were an act.
His perfection was too flawless ever to doubt.
He played his role perfectly, and in the end, he managed to kill even a Root Immortal whole, only at the Spirit Ascension stage.
"I need to break his record.
I must kill an immortal before I reach the Spirit Ascension stage," Kent smiled.
Of all he saw in Faceless’s memories, he was a very meticulous person.
He killed most of his targets from several miles away.
"He was one terrifying accident creator.
He is good, and that was just the first forty-five years of his life." Kent nodded with a satisfied expression.
He never truly understood how some of the kills occurred, but every time Faceless used his brain to kill, it was always successful.
"I was awesome," Kent laughed.
He was very proud of himself.
Not that it wasn’t weird—it was strange—but it was his life, so he could live it however he wanted.
He sighed and then accessed the Faceless Art.
It was a straightforward technique that offered numerous benefits.
First, aside from being able to change his face, he could also alter his voice and even modify his body shape.
It was just like the Perfect Disguise skill Vexthra gave Kent.
However, this one copied the person’s memories and, to some extent, suppressed the user’s memories almost to the point that if they remained in their new persona, they would forget their true self.
It was one terrifying skill that made Kent wonder where his mother had gotten it from.
But in the end, he learned it.
He knew it would come in handy somehow.
He wasn’t planning on becoming the Faceless Assassin.
However, he was also not about to discard such a powerful technique.
He knew it would come in handy one of these days.
"Now, the only thing left for me to do is find a way to get to the immortal worlds so I can kill an immortal and make Faceless’s record obsolete."
He laughed and then lay down, deciding to catch some rest before returning to his training.
It had already been over twenty years since he entered seclusion, and during that time, a great deal had happened.
First, the humans in the tower were all thriving.
They were all powerful cultivators now.
Fifteen years ago, Akira ensured that they all underwent a ritual in which she bestowed upon them some powerful classes.
This was something Kent told her to do.
Afterward, they underwent rigorous training that gradually elevated them to the top, much like the warriors they were meant to be.
Gaia wanted to ensure that the first humans in the tower would one day become beings capable of handling the many races her master would add.
She spared no expense helping them.
Now, they were all training in and out of the dungeons.
As for the Bloodvein Tribe, they were now more monstrous than before.
The tribe chief had raised his chaos affinity to the Perfect stage.
Over the last twenty years, he had undergone two additional evolutions, placing him at the pinnacle of the core formation stage.
Gaia gave him a treasure to strengthen his foundation.
This, of course, involved training inside the dungeons, and as a race known for war and killing, he had improved tremendously.
But he wasn’t the only one.
Hundreds of Bloodvein warriors were growing at a speed many kingdoms would fear.
Then came Kent’s harem.

chapters.title: Chapter 644: Primordial Spirits Awakened [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent’s wives chose to spend a week in Fedora before returning to the tower. When they came back, Kent was deep in seclusion, so they didn’t disturb him.
Instead, they went to the Body Tower and spent five years there, climbing the tower. This was so Princess Lovina could catch up with them.
She already had a strong foundation, so aside from tempering her body with some of the harrowing poisons out there, she was allowed to climb the Golden Titan Stairway just like the rest of them.

It took her three months, but she managed to reach the 30th step, which was the goal. The treasures she found on the 100th, 200th, and 300th steps elevated her to the level of a Silver Body cultivator.
This strengthened her body, and after cultivating for three more months, they all started to climb even further.
Naturally, Unity and Princess Lovina, the two who hadn’t awakened their true names yet, were left in the dust, but that didn’t mean they couldn’t climb.
The gap left behind by their sisters was a couple of dozen steps, but they were slowly catching up.

The goal was to reach the 600th step. It took them five years, but they all reached there, and thanks to the gifts received on the 400th, 500th, and 600th steps, they achieved the Diamond Body in body cultivation.
They were thrilled to the point of wanting to reach the 900th step, but Vexthra took them to their Primordial chambers instead.
Their main target was to awaken their Primordial spirits.
This left only Zaila, who gave them a grin and remained on the stairway. It would take her sisters between 10 and 30 years to awaken their Primordial spirits.
This meant their consciousness would reside in that special place for nearly 30,000 years.
It would be a long time, and it was going to be a very harrowing journey, but they were determined to rise to the occasion and surprise their man when he came out of seclusion.
Their motivation was that they and the Legion would handle the mission on Planet Dusk, while Kent would handle the other things on his shoulders.

Gaia and her sisters might be cheeky sometimes, but when they saw their master had a lot to do and little time to do it all, they went to tell his wives, and this was why they made up their minds to ensure he didn’t carry everything alone.
So they entered the Primordial Chambers with determined smiles.
Years passed, and within those years, Zaila, who had already awakened her Primordial spirit, managed to break into the Sage Body stage in body cultivation after climbing the 800th step.
However, that was where she got stuck. Aside from that, her Primordial spirit, which had started from Tier 1 again, had already reached the 5th Tier.
And that was when the first of her sisters came out of the Primordial Chamber.
It had been seven years since they entered, but Elsa came out with a smile and a cultivation base sitting at the peak of the Core Formation stage.
She had completed all seven core evolutions and awakened a Soul Space. Not that it wasn’t to be expected. Her Primordial Spirit also came out, sitting at the 16th Tier stage in soul cultivation.
Elsa is the Soul Sentinel, so awakening a Soul Space is natural.
However, she ensured that her Primordial spirit underwent the same procedure as Zaila’s, expanding her Soul Space while her primordial spirit regressed to Tier 1.
But this only made her even more powerful. She later joined Zaila on the stairway, who had already reached the 850th step. Elsa spent 7,000 years in the Primordial Chamber.
A year later, Neomi came out dripping red. When she awakened her Primordial spirit and emerged, her sisters shuddered at the sight of her.
She awakened a space called Killing Space. When Elsa and Zaila entered that space, it was like walking into a domain of killers.
Most of the things there had, in one way or another, a property conducive to killing. For example, a certain serene garden inside her Killing Space contained all kinds of poison meant for killing.
It was, without a doubt, very dangerous to look at.
Her Primordial spirit came out sitting at the Tier 17 stage, making her a Spirit Lord. She also dissolved the cultivation base of her primordial spirit, further expanding the Killing Space.
Like Elsa, she emerged at the peak of the Core Formation stage.
A few months after she came out, Ingrid also walked out, radiating the primal energy of the Void. It was a terrifying sight, especially when she walked out with a deep golden panther.
When her True Name was awakened, the tattoo of this Void Creature appeared on her body.
Now, walking out of the Primordial Chamber, the 3-meter-tall golden panther was beside her, and looking into those eyes, it was plain as day that they were the eyes of a predator.
As usual, Ingrid came out sitting at the peak of the Core Formation stage, but so was her beast companion, who could talk and had perfect affinity for the Void.
Ingrid awakened the Void Space, and her Primordial spirit was at the Tier 17 stage. She, of course, came with many gifts, and one of them was the ability to summon the Void Beasts.
However, she had to go back to Tier 1 and start all over again.
Not that it wasn’t for the best.
Because it was for the best, Zaila’s Primordial Spirit was already at Tier 6, but the benefits she was receiving from it were already enough to allow her to stand toe to toe with a Spirit King.
The Primordial spirits were making it possible for the ladies to reach their full potential.
Three weeks after Ingrid came out of the Primordial Chamber, Zaila climbed to the 900th step. However, instead of attaining Nirvana, she broke one limit on her mind and one on her body.
This brought her strength and mental resilience to a whole new level. She became so powerful that she started to climb the Stairs even further.
A year later, Selene emerged from her Primordial Chamber...

chapters.title: Chapter 645: Entering a Deep Sleep
paragraphs: After resting for a bit, Kent decided to get back to work. He planned to go around and check on everyone for a while, but knowing he could ask for help, he used the tower to check on them and then returned to his training.
"The Lost Realm, a place filled with people lost to history and perhaps time itself," Kent muttered, wondering about many things.

The Lost Realm that Faceless talked about piqued his interest, and as someone who had already heard something about worlds going missing, he wanted to one day explore it and see if he could find something.
"I wonder if the long-lost angel race I read about a few years ago would be there." The angel race that went missing with that mysterious swordsman.

The manual titled ’City of Angels’ was one of the random things he received that now starts to make sense. It discussed the disappearance of the Strongest Angel City Race, possibly the original Angel Race.
It was also in the story that he learned about the mysterious swordsman said to have created the ’Starfall’ sword technique.
"What was his name again... Oh, Bob. The one who was able to defeat a clone of mine... millions of years ago, perhaps billions of years ago. I wonder if I will find him there too."
His expectation and interest were already oozing, wondering about so many things to the point he wanted nothing more than to get there fast enough.

In a strange way, he wanted to be there. Even Faceless told him to get where he wanted to go, he must go there, so it wasn’t like Kent’s feelings were unfounded. He knew something wanted him there, so he was going to go one of these days.
"However, Faceless also said I must rise through my weakness and gather strength. That is the only way I will be able to reach my goal.

Chaos also said the same thing, and while I can tell they are asking too much of me, I know they did what they did, so I can have it easy. This also means I must surpass their achievements and prove to myself I still got it."
Kent took a deep sigh and then decided on the path he would follow next.

"I have already completed the memories, and that alone gave me the strength to roam a High World freely. But while that is good, I am not the only monster out there, so to be self-assured, I must complete my plans.
Next, I need to awaken my Soul Path. That is the only way for me to use my soul cultivation much more efficiently.
I have already seen what Elsa can do, and while she is only at Tier 12 in soul cultivation, if not for my soul immunity, I wouldn’t stand a chance against her."
Kent sighed, his mind drifting back to his wife, who had already made sure his soul was free from harm.
Elsa helped him become someone who could use soul attacks, but the same attacks would never hurt him. Talk about a good wife.
"I’d better get on that for now. Who knows what kind of gift is waiting for me?" Kent smiled and then readied himself. He vanished and appeared inside the Soul Tower.
"Okay, Akira, I am ready." The Soul Weaver appeared along with Gaia and Dori. Since this involves the soul, a Soul Weaver is required.
"So, how is it going to be?" Kent asked, staring at his three assistants.

⟪The skill is buried deep within your soul. As I said, I don’t know where she got it, but I have to say, the process will take some time, and while I love to estimate, you will be looking at a range of 10 to 60 years.
The reason is simple: the stronger your soul, the more tedious it is to awaken this path, so for now, you have to relax and be out for a while.
Your soul is already at the Tier 13 stage.⟫
"So I will be unconscious for that long, huh?" Akira and her sisters nodded. Kent sighed and glared at them.

"I know you three have something planned. I won’t tell you not to do it, but know this: if I wake up and find out you did something to my body, you better prepare your bumbums because I will spank you silly."
The three lolis giggled, hearing what their master was saying.
⟪Don’t worry, master, we don’t have anything planned, so be assured.⟫
"Good," Kent smiled and then readied himself. However, before he could ask Akira to go ahead, a message appeared on his screen, bringing a smile to his face.
⟦Your servant, Jacob Ashland, has a trust level of 80%. You can now invoke his True Name and unleash his true potential.⟧
"Ladies, I have a mission for you three," Kent said, and the three lolis became very happy hearing that.
⟪What kind of mission, Master?⟫ they asked.
"I want you to locate my first servant, Jacob, and bring him to the tower. I can ask the tower to teleport him here, but since you three are bored, why don’t you take a walk outside for a few weeks?
You can even decide not to use your abilities and look for him like a mundane. This way, by the time you get back, I will be nearing the completion of my Soul Path awakening.
What do you think?"
⟪Rest assured, Master, we will get it done⟫. They were so happy that Kent could see the smiles on their faces and how much they wanted to get down to business quickly.
"Then let’s get down to business here first." Akira nodded and laid Kent on his back. Then she pressed her finger on his forehead, and before Kent knew it, his eyes turned hazy and he passed out.
The three lolis looked at his sleeping face, and smiles appeared on their faces.
⟪Such a beautiful face. Drawing all over it wouldn’t be a waste at all⟫, Gaia said, and her sisters nodded.
⟪Let’s get the mission on the road first. I have a feeling we will come back to a different version of Master, one that will shock even us.⟫
Dori and her sisters left the tower immediately and began searching for Jacob Ashland.

Though Kent never looked for him after leaving him with the money to handle his cultivation and a few items to keep him safe, it seemed Jacob had finally gathered some trust in Kent, and now, his true potential would be unleashed.
But until then, Kent was on a journey to awaken his Soul Path.
